summary: Algebraic cycles, pure and mixed motives, planned from four freely available sources read in full for the parts used: the Stacks Project's chapter on Weil cohomology theories for correspondences, Chow motives and the axiomatics of a realisation; Jannsen's 1992 paper, read from the author's institutional repository, for the semisimplicity of numerical motives; Huber and Mueller-Stach's paper on Nori motives and Kontsevich periods for the diagram construction and the formal period torsor; and Mazza, Voevodsky and Weibel's Clay lecture notes for the geometric mixed motives that survive the narrowing RS-08 imposes on MC.4. MC.0 builds the graded category of correspondences over Q and the equivalence relations; MC.1 builds the Chow motives with their tensor structure, twists, duality, Chow groups and the projective bundle formula; MC.2 owns what a realisation is, ending in the equivalence between classical Weil cohomology theories and Q-linear symmetric monoidal functors on motives; MC.3 is Jannsen's theorem with the trace formula, the Wedderburn lemma, the dual numbers non-example, the radical computation and the Tannakian conclusion after the sign change; MC.4 is left partial and plans only what RS-08 assigns it, importing the cycle complexes from MotivicEtaleKTheory:M.4 and the finite correspondences, the effective category and cancellation from M.5a; MC.5 and MC.6 build Nori's diagram categories, the motivic Galois group and the torsor of formal periods; MC.7 is left partial with the two conjectures the sources state precisely and the register of known cases, and with the Hodge and Tate conjectures named as remaining rather than written from memory. The Chow groups themselves, the intersection product and every cohomology theory are imported through six requests and are planned nowhere in this packet.

declarations.provides: Algebraic cycles on a scheme as locally finite integer combinations of points. This is the whole of what the pinned libraries have towards cycles: there is no rational equivalence and no Chow group, which is why the Chow groups this roadmap uses are imported from SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5 rather than planned here.

Pushforward of an algebraic cycle along a quasi-compact morphism, with residue-degree multiplicities. Only map_id is proved; functoriality and compatibility with rational equivalence are not, which is part of what SF.5 owes this roadmap.

Properness of a morphism of schemes. Projectivity is not in the pinned libraries; properness is what the pushforward of cycles and the trace maps actually use, and it is what the hypotheses below are stated against.
The category of schemes. Every object of this roadmap is indexed by smooth projective schemes over a field, so this is the carrier every statement below is parametrised by.
Smoothness of a morphism of schemes as a morphism property. The standing hypothesis 'X smooth over k' is this property for the structure morphism.
Bialgebras over a commutative semiring; the hypothesis of MC.6/rigid-bialgebra-is-hopf.
declarations.checked: statement read at the pinned commit by REV-MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles (R4)

sources.title: The Hodge Conjecture
sources.edition: The Clay Mathematics Institute's official problem description for the Millennium Prize Problem, 5 pages
readSections: Section 1 (Statement), read in full: the Hodge decomposition and the Hodge filtration with Griffiths transversality, the construction of the class of a closed analytic subspace through the integration current, the definition of a Hodge class and the statement of the conjecture.

Section 2 (Remarks), read in full: Chow's theorem, the formulation through Chern classes of algebraic vector bundles, the proved case of degree two through the exponential sequence, the failure of the integral statement in the Atiyah-Hirzebruch filtration, the complex-torus counterexample to the Kaehler generalisation, and Grothendieck's observation on Hodge's further conjecture.

Section 3 (The Intermediate Jacobian) and Section 4 (Detecting Hodge Classes), read: the lift of the cycle class to the intermediate Jacobian, the sub-Hodge structure generated by algebraic cycles, and the absence of an algorithm for deciding whether a class is a Hodge class.

readSections: Section 1 (Origins of the Tate conjecture), read in full: the l-adic cohomology used, the Tate twist, the cycle class of a subvariety, Conjecture 1.1, the necessity of the hypothesis on the base field, the relation to the finiteness of the Tate-Shafarevich group, the analogy with the Hodge conjecture, and the summary diagram of implications.

Section 2 (The broader context: variants of the Tate conjecture), read in full: the strong Tate conjecture and its consequences for the standard conjectures, Jannsen's Borel-Moore variant, the reduction along a finite extension of the base field, the variant over the separable closure, the integral Tate conjecture, the Tate-Beilinson conjecture, and the consequence of the strong conjecture for the category of motives over a finite field.

Section 3 (First results over finite fields), read in full: Tate's theorem for divisors on abelian varieties with its equivalent formulation in terms of homomorphisms and Tate modules, Zarhin's trick and the finiteness of the moduli of principally polarised abelian varieties.

Sections 4 and 5, read: the Kuga-Satake correspondence, Andre's theorem for hyperkaehler varieties over number fields, Moonen's Theorem 4.1 with its hypotheses, the definitions of a K3 surface and of supersingularity, the elliptic case of Artin and Swinnerton-Dyer through the finiteness of the Tate-Shafarevich group, and the attribution of the supersingular case.

sources.title: Cancellation theorem
sources.edition: arXiv:math/0202012v1, 1 February 2002; read from the arXiv e-print LaTeX source canarch.tex
readSections: The main theorem and its proof outline: for a presheaf with transfers admitting an epimorphism from a scheme, every morphism from the smash of the Tate circle with it to the smash of the Tate circle with a scheme is, uniquely up to A^1-homotopy, the smash of the identity with a morphism.
The corollary identifying a scheme with the internal Hom presheaf from the Tate circle to its smash with the Tate circle, at the level of Suslin complexes.

The final corollary: for a PERFECT field k and any K, L in the triangulated category of effective motives, the map Hom(K,L) -> Hom(K(1),L(1)) is a bijection; this is the cancellation theorem without a resolution-of-singularities hypothesis.

The e-print source archive has SHA-256 0a8fe209fed447b21006c9251e3cf37141d3f0da147f313b9223d3be57d0a46e. Not read: the technical sections on the operators rho_n and the lemmas supporting the main theorem.

nodes.title: Correspondences of degree r
nodes.statement: Let k be a field and let X and Y be smooth projective schemes over k. Write X as the disjoint union of its open and closed parts X_d that are equidimensional of dimension d. For an integer r define the Q-vector space of correspondences of degree r from X to Y as the direct sum over d of CH^{d+r}(X_d times Y) tensored with Q, viewed inside CH^*(X times Y) tensor Q. The grading is by codimension on each equidimensional part, and the shift by d is what makes the degree of a graph equal to zero whatever the dimension of X.
hypotheses: k is a field.

X and Y are smooth projective schemes over k, not assumed equidimensional or connected. Every argument of MC.0 and MC.1 uses only that X and Y are smooth and proper over k: flatness of the projections from products, proper pushforward and the intersection product on smooth schemes. The pinned libraries have properness (AlgebraicGeometry.IsProper) but no notion of a projective morphism, so a formalisation may index the theory by smooth proper schemes over k; that category contains the smooth projective schemes of the source and every statement of the two layers holds for it unchanged.

Chow groups are taken with rational coefficients. The integral Chow groups CH^i are imported from SF.5 and tensored with Q here, so the integral groups are retained upstream of this definition, as the layer's boundary requires.
proofSteps: Decompose X into the open and closed subschemes X_d equidimensional of dimension d; this decomposition is finite and canonical.
For each d take CH^{d+r}(X_d times Y) tensor Q and form the direct sum over d.
Check that the sum embeds in CH^*(X times Y) tensor Q, so a correspondence is a rational cycle class on the product and nothing more.
Record that degree zero is the degree of a graph: for a morphism from Y to X the graph meets X_d times Y in pure codimension d.
acceptance: For X equidimensional of dimension d the group of correspondences of degree r from X to Y is CH^{d+r}(X times Y) tensor Q; a definition that forgets the shift by d fails this already for X a point against X a curve.
For X the spectrum of k the group of correspondences of degree r from X to Y is CH^r(Y) tensor Q.
The group is a Q-vector space and vanishes for r outside a finite range determined by the dimensions of X and Y.

nodes.title: Pullback and pushforward of cycles by a correspondence
nodes.statement: Let c be a correspondence of degree r from X to Y. For a cycle class b in CH_j(Y) tensor Q define the pullback of b by c to be the pushforward along the first projection of the intersection product of c with the pullback of b along the second projection; it lies in CH_{j-r}(X) tensor Q. For a cycle class a in CH^i(X) tensor Q define the pushforward of a by c to be the pushforward along the second projection of the intersection product of c with the pullback of a along the first projection; it lies in CH^{i+r}(Y) tensor Q. Both are Q-linear in the cycle and in c.
hypotheses: X and Y are smooth projective over k, so that the projections from X times Y are proper and flat on each equidimensional part.
c is a correspondence of degree r from X to Y.
Cycle classes are rational.
proofSteps: Check that the second projection restricted to X_d times Y is flat of relative dimension d, so that the flat pullback of a cycle of dimension j is a cycle of dimension d + j.
Intersect with c, which lies in codimension d + r on X_d times Y, to land in dimension j - r.
Push forward along the first projection, which is proper, preserving dimension, and conclude that the pullback lands in CH_{j-r}(X) tensor Q.

Repeat the bookkeeping in codimension for the pushforward: the first projection pullback of a class of codimension i has codimension i, the product with c has codimension i + d + r on X_d times Y, and the proper pushforward along the second projection lands in codimension i + r on Y.
Prove Q-bilinearity of both operations in c and in the cycle, from linearity of flat pullback, proper pushforward and the intersection product.
acceptance: The degrees are as stated: pullback lowers dimension by r and pushforward raises codimension by r. An implementation that keeps the degree fixed is wrong.
For c the class of the diagonal both operations are the identity.
Both operations are Q-linear in the cycle and in the correspondence.

sources.locator: Section 0FFZ, the two displayed formulas after the definition of Corr^r(X, Y)
sources.excerpt: Given c in Corr^r(X, Y) and b in CH_j(Y) tensor Q we can define the pullback of b by c using the formula c^*(b) = pr_{1,*}(c . pr_2^*b) in CH_{j-r}(X) tensor Q. Similarly, switching to grading by codimension, given a in CH^i(X) tensor Q, c_*(a) = pr_{2,*}(c . pr_1^*a) in CH^{i+r}(Y) tensor Q.
sources.match: The node is those two formulas together with the dimension bookkeeping the source gives immediately after each, which is what fixes the target degrees.

nodes.title: Composition of correspondences through the triple product
nodes.statement: For smooth projective X, Y, Z over k define a Q-bilinear composition from correspondences of degree s from Y to Z and correspondences of degree r from X to Y to correspondences of degree r + s from X to Z by sending a pair (c', c) to the pushforward along the projection from X times Y times Z to X times Z of the intersection product of the pullback of c along the projection to X times Y with the pullback of c' along the projection to Y times Z.
hypotheses: X, Y and Z are smooth projective schemes over k.
c is a correspondence of degree r from X to Y and c' one of degree s from Y to Z.
The three projections from the triple product are used: the first two are flat on each equidimensional part and the projection to X times Z is proper.
proofSteps: Pull c back along the projection to X times Y and c' back along the projection to Y times Z, both flat pullbacks on each equidimensional piece.
Take the intersection product of the two pulled back classes on the triple product.
Push the result forward along the proper projection to X times Z.
Check the degree: the result has degree r + s, by the same dimension count as for the action on cycles.
Check Q-bilinearity, from linearity of flat pullback, proper pushforward and the intersection product.
acceptance: Composition is Q-bilinear and raises degree additively.
Composing the graphs of two composable morphisms gives the graph of the composite, in the opposite order.
Composition with the class of the diagonal on either side is the identity.

nodes.title: Composition of correspondences is bilinear and associative
nodes.statement: Composition of correspondences is Q-bilinear and associative: for smooth projective X, Y, Z, W over k and c in Corr^r(X, Y), c' in Corr^s(Y, Z), c'' in Corr^t(Z, W) one has c'' o (c' o c) = (c'' o c') o c in Corr^{r+s+t}(X, W).
hypotheses: X, Y, Z and W are smooth projective over k.
All cycle classes are rational.
proofSteps: Bilinearity: from the linearity of flat pullback and proper pushforward and the bilinearity of the intersection product.

Expand c'' o (c' o c) on X × Y × Z × W in five equalities, as the source does: (i) the definition of composition; (ii) flat pullback along pr^{134}_{13} after proper pushforward along pr^{123}_{13} equals proper pushforward along pr^{1234}_{134} after flat pullback along pr^{1234}_{123}, for the fibre square of projections (Stacks 02RG); (iii) flat pullback along pr^{1234}_{123} commutes with the intersection product (Stacks 0FFB, with 0FF4 identifying the Gysin map of a flat morphism with flat pullback), together with functoriality of flat pullback for the composite projections; (iv) the projection formula for pr^{1234}_{134} (Stacks 0FFC), again with functoriality of flat pullback; (v) functoriality of proper pushforward (Stacks 02R5).

The result is pr^{1234}_{14,*}((pr_{12}^*c . pr_{23}^*c') . pr_{34}^*c''). The same five steps applied to (c'' o c') o c give pr^{1234}_{14,*}(pr_{12}^*c . (pr_{23}^*c' . pr_{34}^*c'')), and associativity of the intersection product (Stacks 0FC1) identifies the two.
The source labels the justification of step (v) as a second 'fourth equality' (sourceIssues MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles/E3); the five justifications are the ones listed here.
acceptance: Associativity is an equality of correspondences of degree r + s + t, not merely of their actions on cycles.
Bilinearity holds in each argument separately.
On the projective line with the projectors c_0 and c_2 of Example 0FG6, both bracketings of c_2 o c_0 o c_2 are zero and both bracketings of c_0 o c_0 o c_0 are c_0.

nodes.title: The graph of a morphism as a correspondence of degree zero
nodes.statement: Let f be a morphism from Y to X of smooth projective schemes over k and let the graph of f be the image of the closed immersion (f, identity) from Y into X times Y. Then the intersection of the graph with X_d times Y has pure codimension d for every d, so the class of the graph is a correspondence of degree zero from X to Y.
hypotheses: f is a morphism of smooth projective schemes over k, from Y to X.
X is decomposed into its equidimensional parts X_d.
proofSteps: Show that (f, identity) is a closed immersion, since its composite with the second projection is the identity.

Compute the dimension of the graph over each part: the intersection of the graph with X_d times Y is isomorphic to the preimage of X_d in Y, of dimension equal to that of that preimage, so its codimension in X_d times Y is d.
Conclude that the class of the graph lies in CH^d(X_d times Y) tensor Q for each d, that is, in degree zero.
acceptance: The degree is zero for every f, independently of the dimensions of X and Y.
For f the identity the graph is the diagonal.
The construction is compatible with composition in the reverse order, which is the content of the functoriality statement.

sources.excerpt: Let f : Y to X be a morphism of smooth projective schemes over k. Denote Gamma_f in X times Y the graph of f. [...] Then Gamma_f intersected with X_d times Y has pure codimension d. Hence [Gamma_f] [...] is contained in Corr^0(X times Y), i.e., [Gamma_f] is a correspondence of degree 0 from X to Y.
sources.match: The node is that example, with the codimension computation made a proof step. The source's 'Corr^0(X times Y)' is a misprint for Corr^0(X, Y) (sourceIssues MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles/E6); the node uses the corrected group.

nodes.title: The graded category of correspondences
nodes.statement: Smooth projective schemes over k, with the groups of correspondences as graded morphism spaces and the composition above, form a graded category over Q. The identity of X is the class of the diagonal of X, which is the graph of the identity morphism.
hypotheses: k is a field.
Objects are smooth projective schemes over k; morphism spaces are the graded correspondence groups.
proofSteps: Take bilinearity and associativity of composition from the composition lemma.

For the identity, prove that composing the class of the diagonal with an arbitrary correspondence gives back that correspondence. Reduce to the class of an integral closed subscheme Z of X times Y, then to X and Y integral.

Identify the image of Z under the map (diagonal, identity) with the scheme theoretic intersection of the diagonal times Y with X times Z inside X times X times Y, check that the dimensions add up to a proper intersection and that the generic point has Cohen-Macaulay local rings, and apply the proper intersection formula to identify the intersection product with the class of that image.
Push forward along the projection to X times Y, which maps that image isomorphically to Z, and conclude.
Repeat on the other side.
acceptance: The diagonal class is a two-sided identity, not only an identity on the action on cycles.
Composition is associative and bilinear, so the data is a graded category over Q.
The morphism spaces in each degree are Q-vector spaces and the composition respects the grading additively.

sources.excerpt: Smooth projective schemes over k with correspondences and composition of correspondences as defined above form a graded category over Q [...]. Everything is clear from the construction and Lemma 0FG0 except for the existence of identity morphisms.

nodes.title: The contravariant functor from schemes to correspondences
nodes.statement: There is a contravariant functor from the category of smooth projective schemes over k to the degree zero part of the category of correspondences which is the identity on objects and sends a morphism f from Y to X to the class of its graph, a correspondence of degree zero from X to Y.
hypotheses: f and g are morphisms of smooth projective schemes over k, with g from Z to Y and f from Y to X.
proofSteps: Identities go to identities, because the graph of the identity is the diagonal.

For composites, reduce as in the identity axiom to X, Y and Z integral and show that the composite of the two graph classes is the pushforward along the projection to X times Z of the intersection product of the graph of f times Z with X times the graph of g.
Identify that intersection scheme theoretically with the image of Z under the map (f after g, g, identity), check the proper intersection hypotheses and apply the proper intersection formula.
Push forward along the projection to X times Z and identify the result with the graph of f after g.

It is the identity on objects, so it does not change the indexing of the theory.

nodes.title: The transpose of a correspondence
nodes.statement: Let X be equidimensional of dimension d and Y equidimensional of dimension e, both smooth projective over k. The isomorphism from X times Y to Y times X switching the factors induces an isomorphism from the correspondences of degree r from X to Y to the correspondences of degree d - e + r from Y to X, called the transpose. It is defined on cycles as well as on cycle classes, and the transpose of the graph of a morphism f from Y to X is the transposed graph.
hypotheses: X and Y are smooth projective over k and equidimensional, of dimensions d and e; the transpose is not defined by this formula without equidimensionality.
r is an integer.
proofSteps: Take the isomorphism of schemes switching the two factors and its induced isomorphism on Chow groups.
Compute the effect on the grading: a class of codimension d + r on X times Y becomes a class of codimension d + r on Y times X, which is codimension e + (d - e + r), that is, degree d - e + r.
Record that the construction is defined on cycles and descends to classes, since the switch is an isomorphism of schemes.
Check the effect on graphs.
acceptance: The degree shift is d - e + r and not r; for X a surface and Y a curve the transpose of a degree zero correspondence has degree one.
The transpose is an isomorphism of Q-vector spaces and is an involution up to the degree bookkeeping.
The transpose of the graph of f is the transposed graph of f.

It acts on cycles as well as cycle classes.

nodes.title: What the graph and the transposed graph do to cycles
nodes.statement: Let f be a morphism from Y to X of smooth projective schemes over k. Pushforward of cycles by the correspondence given by the graph of f agrees with the Gysin map from CH^*(X) to CH^*(Y), and pullback of cycles by that correspondence agrees with the proper pushforward from CH_*(Y) to CH_*(X). If moreover X and Y are equidimensional of dimensions d and e, then pushforward by the transposed graph is the proper pushforward along f and pullback by the transposed graph is the Gysin map.
hypotheses: f is a morphism of smooth projective schemes over k.
For the last two statements X and Y are equidimensional.
proofSteps: Expand the pushforward by the graph: [Gamma_f]_*(alpha) = pr_{2,*}([Gamma_f] . pr_1^*alpha).
Intersecting with the class of the regularly embedded Gamma_f is (f, 1)_* of the Gysin map of (f, 1) (Stacks 0FFE): [Gamma_f] . pr_1^*alpha = (f, 1)_*((f, 1)^! pr_1^*alpha).
The Gysin map of the flat pr_1 is flat pullback (Stacks 0FF4) and Gysin maps compose (Stacks 0FF5); since pr_1 o (f, 1) = f this is (f, 1)_*(f^! alpha).
Conclude with pr_{2,*} o (f, 1)_* = id (Stacks 02R5), which gives part (1).

For part (2) the same computation with pr_2 gives [Gamma_f] . pr_2^*beta = (f, 1)_*beta, whose pushforward by pr_1 is f_*beta; the source writes the pullback here with a lower star (sourceIssues MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles/E4).
Part (3) is the same computation after transposing, for X and Y equidimensional.
acceptance: The four statements pair up as stated: the graph gives the Gysin map in one direction and the proper pushforward in the other, and the transposed graph exchanges them.
For f a closed immersion of a point in the projective line the graph recovers the restriction of a cycle class to the point, and the transposed graph recovers the class of the point.
Each statement is an equality of maps on Chow groups with rational coefficients.

nodes.title: The symmetric monoidal structure on correspondences
nodes.statement: Define the tensor product of two smooth projective schemes to be their product over k, and the tensor product of a correspondence of degree r from X to Y with a correspondence of degree r' from X' to Y' to be the intersection product on the fourfold product of the pullback of the first along the projection to X times Y with the pullback of the second along the projection to X' times Y'; it is a correspondence of degree r + r' from X times X' to Y times Y'. With the usual associativity constraint of products of schemes and the switch of factors as commutativity constraint this makes the category of correspondences symmetric monoidal with unit the spectrum of k.
hypotheses: X, X', Y and Y' are smooth projective over k.
The four projections from the fourfold product are the ones used, and the pullbacks are flat pullbacks on equidimensional parts.
proofSteps: Define the tensor product on objects as the product of schemes and on morphisms by c tensor c' = pr_{13}^*c . pr_{24}^*c'.
Check the degree: the product of a class of degree r and one of degree r' has degree r + r'.
Bifunctoriality and the value on graphs and diagonals are the interchange lemma MC.0/tensor-interchange.

Take the associativity constraint from the associativity of products of schemes and the commutativity constraint from the switch of factors, both as graphs of isomorphisms of schemes; their naturality with respect to correspondences follows from the interchange lemma and the fact that the graph of an isomorphism acts by transport of cycles; the pentagon and hexagon axioms hold because they hold for the underlying isomorphisms of schemes and the graph functor is a functor.

Check that Spec(k) is a unit, the unitors being graphs of the canonical isomorphisms X × Spec(k) = X = Spec(k) × X, and that the tensor product is Q-bilinear on morphisms, so that the degree zero category is monoidal linear over Q.
acceptance: The unit is the spectrum of k and the tensor product of objects is the product of schemes.
The tensor product of graphs is the graph of the product morphism.
The commutativity constraint is the switch, so the structure is symmetric and not merely braided.

nodes.title: The two orthogonal projectors on the projective line
nodes.statement: Let X be the projective line over k and let x be a k-rational point. Inside the degree zero correspondences from X to X, which are CH^1(X times X) tensor Q, put c_0 the class of x times X and c_2 the class of X times x. Then the class of the diagonal is c_0 + c_2, the four composites satisfy c_0 after c_0 = c_0, c_2 after c_2 = c_2 and both mixed composites vanish, and the algebra of degree zero endomorphisms of X is the product of two copies of Q.
hypotheses: k is a field and X is the projective line over k.
x is a k-rational point of X.
proofSteps: Compute CH^1(X × X) tensor Q for X = P^1 from the projective bundle formula for Chow groups (Stacks 02TX, imported from SF.5) applied to the projection X × X -> X, and exhibit the classes of x × X and X × x as a basis.
Write the diagonal in that basis by intersecting with the two basis classes: [Delta] . [x × X] and [Delta] . [X × x] are both the class of the point (x, x), of degree one, so [Delta] = c_0 + c_2.

Compute the four composites on X × X × X. For c_0 o c_0 and c_2 o c_2 the two pulled back classes meet transversally in x × x × X, respectively X × x × x, which pr_13 maps isomorphically onto x × X, respectively X × x, so each is idempotent.
c_2 o c_0 = pr_{13,*}([x × X × X] . [X × X × x]) = pr_{13,*}[x × X × x] vanishes because pr_13 contracts the curve x × X × x to a point, so the proper pushforward of its class is zero.

c_0 o c_2 = pr_{13,*}([X × x × X] . [X × x × X]) is a self-intersection that is not proper: it equals the flat pullback along pr_2 of [x] . [x] in CH^2(X) = 0, so it vanishes for dimension reasons and not because of a pushforward.
Conclude that c_0 and c_2 are orthogonal idempotents summing to the identity and that Corr^0(X, X) is Q × Q as a Q-algebra.
acceptance: The diagonal is the sum of the two classes, which is the acceptance test of the layer for projective space.
The two mixed composites vanish and the two pure ones are idempotent; a computation that returns a nonzero mixed composite has made a dimension error.
The endomorphism algebra is two-dimensional, not one-dimensional: the projective line is not indecomposable as a correspondence object.

nodes.title: The three orthogonal projectors on a pointed smooth projective curve
nodes.statement: Let C be a geometrically irreducible smooth projective curve over k with a k-rational point e. Inside the degree zero correspondences from C to C put p_0 the class of e times C and p_2 the class of C times e. Then p_0 and p_2 are orthogonal idempotents, p_1 defined as the class of the diagonal minus p_0 minus p_2 is an idempotent orthogonal to both, and the three sum to the class of the diagonal.
hypotheses: k is a field, C is a geometrically irreducible smooth projective curve over k and e is a k-rational point of C.
Degree zero correspondences from C to C are CH^1(C times C) tensor Q.
proofSteps: Identify p_0 = [e × C] with the composite of the graph of the point e : Spec(k) -> C, a correspondence of degree zero from C to Spec(k), followed by the graph of the structure morphism C -> Spec(k), a correspondence of degree zero from Spec(k) to C, exactly as in the proof of Lemma 0FGD; and p_2 = [C × e] with its transpose, of degree 1 - 1 + 0 = 0.

p_0 o p_0 = p_0 and p_2 o p_2 = p_2: the pulled back classes meet transversally in e × e × C, respectively C × e × e, which pr_13 maps isomorphically onto e × C, respectively C × e; this uses that e is a rational point.
p_2 o p_0 = pr_{13,*}[e × C × e] = 0 because pr_13 contracts the curve e × C × e to a point.
p_0 o p_2 = pr_{13,*}([C × e × C] . [C × e × C]) is a non-proper self-intersection; it is the flat pullback along pr_2 of [e] . [e] in CH^2(C) = 0, hence zero.
Define p_1 = [Delta] - p_0 - p_2 and check idempotence and orthogonality from the previous steps and the fact that [Delta] is the identity.
Record that the three classes sum to [Delta] by construction, so that they are a complete orthogonal family.
acceptance: The three classes are orthogonal idempotents summing to the identity, which is the layer's acceptance test for a pointed curve.
p_1 is not zero unless the curve has genus zero; for the projective line with e the chosen point p_1 vanishes and the family reduces to the two projectors of the previous node.
The construction depends on the chosen rational point: a different point changes p_0 and p_2, and it changes p_1 by a correspondence that is not in general zero.

nodes.title: Adequate equivalence relations on algebraic cycles
nodes.statement: Fix a field F of characteristic zero. An adequate equivalence relation on F-linear cycles on smooth projective schemes over k is recorded by the classes it identifies with zero: a family I of graded F-subspaces I^*(X) of CH^*(X) tensor F, one for each smooth projective X over k, such that (a) f^*(I^*(X)) is contained in I^*(Y) for every morphism f : Y -> X; (b) f_*(I(Y)) is contained in I(X) for every morphism f : Y -> X, pushforward being taken on dimension-graded Chow groups; and (c) alpha . beta lies in I^*(X) whenever alpha lies in I^*(X) and beta in CH^*(X) tensor F. Write A^j(X) = A^j(X, F) = (CH^j(X) tensor F)/I^j(X). Two F-linear cycles are equivalent when the difference of their classes lies in I. Rational equivalence is the family I = 0 and is finer than every adequate relation; the trivial relation, I^*(X) = CH^*(X) tensor F for every X, is adequate as well.
hypotheses: k is a field and F a field of characteristic zero; the Chow groups CH^*(X) are the integral ones imported from SF.5.

Jannsen defines adequacy on cycles, following Samuel and Kleiman: pullback, pushforward and intersection of cycles are well defined modulo the relation. The relations of that kind which are coarser than rational equivalence, the only ones any consumer in this roadmap uses, are the same data as the families of the statement. The family form is the one a formalisation can state, since the intersection of two cycles is defined only when they meet properly.
The trivial relation, which identifies every class with zero, satisfies the three conditions; every statement comparing adequate relations with numerical equivalence must exclude it.
proofSteps: Record the three closure conditions (a), (b), (c) as the definition of an adequate family.

Deduce stability under exterior products, alpha × beta = pr_1^*alpha . pr_2^*beta, from (a) and (c), and stability under the action of any correspondence, c_*(alpha) = pr_{2,*}(c . pr_1^*alpha), from (a), (b) and (c).

Define A^j(X) and check that composition and tensor product of correspondences descend: in c' o c = pr_{13,*}(pr_{12}^*c . pr_{23}^*c') a factor lying in I stays in I under the pullbacks (a), the product (c) and the pushforward (b).

Record that I = 0 (rational equivalence) and I = everything (the trivial relation) are adequate, that I = 0 is contained in every adequate family, and that the adequate families are closed under sums and intersections.
acceptance: The three closure conditions are part of the definition. Without condition (b) the family of all classes of positive codimension would qualify, and composition of correspondences would not descend to the quotient.
Rational equivalence (I = 0) is adequate and finer than every adequate relation.
The trivial relation is adequate; no statement of this roadmap may claim that every adequate relation is finer than numerical equivalence without excluding it.
The coefficient field F is a parameter: A^j(X, F) for different F are different groups.

For a variety X and an integer j ≥ 0, denote by A^j(X) = A^j(X, F) the group

nodes.title: Numerical equivalence
nodes.statement: Let F be a field of characteristic zero and X a smooth projective scheme over k. The degree pairing sends alpha in CH^j(X) tensor F and beta in CH_j(X) tensor F to deg(alpha . beta) in F, the degree over k of the zero-cycle class alpha . beta. A class alpha is numerically trivial if deg(alpha . beta) = 0 for every beta in CH_j(X) tensor F, and two F-linear cycles are numerically equivalent if the difference of their classes is numerically trivial. The numerically trivial classes form an adequate family, so the quotient A_num^*(X) is a graded ring, a quotient of the Chow ring tensor F. An adequate family I with I^0(Spec(k)) = 0 consists of numerically trivial classes, and an adequate family with I^0(Spec(k)) nonzero is the trivial relation; so numerical equivalence is the coarsest adequate relation other than the trivial one.
hypotheses: X is a smooth projective scheme over k; for X not equidimensional the pairing is taken on each equidimensional part, which is what grading beta by dimension does.

Intersection numbers are degrees over k of zero-cycle classes (the degree deg : CH_0(X) -> Z of SF.5, extended F-linearly). They are computed on Chow groups, where every pair of classes has a product; Milne's 'for which the intersection numbers are defined' refers to cycles.
Coefficients are F-linear as in the adequate relation definition.
proofSteps: Define the pairing from the intersection product and the degree of zero cycles (SF.5).

Stability under pullback: for f : Y -> X and beta on Y, deg(f^*alpha . beta) = deg(f_*(f^*alpha . beta)) = deg(alpha . f_*beta) = 0, by the projection formula and the compatibility of the degree with proper pushforward.
Stability under pushforward: deg(f_*gamma . beta) = deg(gamma . f^*beta) = 0, by the projection formula.
Stability under products: deg((alpha . gamma) . beta) = deg(alpha . (gamma . beta)) = 0, by associativity and commutativity of the intersection product.

Comparison: let I be adequate with I^0(Spec(k)) = 0 and alpha in I^j(X); for beta in CH_j(X) tensor F, alpha . beta lies in I by (c), and its pushforward to Spec(k), which is deg(alpha . beta) times [Spec(k)], lies in I^0(Spec(k)) = 0 by (b); so alpha is numerically trivial. If instead I^0(Spec(k)) is nonzero it contains [Spec(k)], so [X] = pi^*[Spec(k)] lies in I^0(X) for every X by (a), and then I is everything by (c).
acceptance: The test is against all classes of complementary dimension, not against a chosen realisation; equality of cohomology classes is a different relation.
The quotient is a ring, so numerical equivalence is compatible with the intersection product.
On a connected smooth projective curve numerical equivalence of zero cycles is equality of degrees.
The comparison with other adequate relations excludes the trivial relation, which is adequate and strictly coarser than numerical equivalence.

sources.excerpt: The coarsest such equivalence relation is numerical equivalence: two algebraic cycles γ and γ′ are numerically equivalent if γ · δ = γ′ · δ for all algebraic cycles δ of complementary dimension for which the intersection numbers are defined.
sources.match: The node is that definition, stated on Chow groups with F-coefficients; Milne's next sentence, that the classes form a ring which is a quotient of the Chow ring, is the ring structure.

nodes.title: Homological equivalence relative to a chosen Weil cohomology
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed and H a classical Weil cohomology theory over k with coefficients in a field Lambda of characteristic zero, and let F be a field of characteristic zero such that Lambda is an F-algebra, so that the cycle class map gamma_X : CH^j(X) -> H^{2j}(X) extends F-linearly to CH^j(X) tensor F. A class alpha in CH^j(X) tensor F on a smooth projective scheme X over k is homologically trivial for H if gamma(alpha) = 0 on every connected component of X. The homologically trivial classes form an adequate family I_H, written ~_H; it contains no multiple of [Spec(k)] other than zero, and every homologically trivial class is numerically trivial. The relation depends on H. Over a field k that is not algebraically closed, homological equivalence relative to H is defined through the base change of MC.2/weil-cohomology-by-base-change: a class on X is homologically trivial when its base change to X_{k̄} is (API item WeilCohomology.baseChange_homEquiv).
hypotheses: k is algebraically closed, as for the classical Weil cohomology theories MC.2 plans (Stacks, Section 0FGS). Jannsen uses homological equivalence over an arbitrary field k, through etale cohomology of X over a separable closure; that needs the Weil cohomology theories of Stacks Definition 0FI2, which no node of this packet plans (recorded as a gap).
H is a classical Weil cohomology theory over k with coefficients in Lambda, and Lambda is an algebra over the coefficient field F of the cycle groups; Jannsen imposes the same condition.
A classical theory is defined on varieties; on a smooth projective scheme over the algebraically closed field k the relation is taken on each connected component, which is a variety.
proofSteps: Define I_H^j(X) as the kernel of the F-linear extension of gamma on each connected component of X.

Adequacy: axiom (C)(a) gives stability under pullback; axiom (C)(b), with the cohomological pushforward defined from Poincaré duality (MC.2/weil-pushforward), gives stability under pushforward; axiom (C)(c) gives stability under products with arbitrary classes.

Homological triviality implies numerical triviality: for alpha in I_H^j(X) and beta in CH_j(X) tensor F, deg(alpha . beta) = the trace of gamma(alpha . beta) = the trace of gamma(alpha) cup gamma(beta) = 0, by the degree lemma MC.2/cycle-class-degree and axiom (C)(c).
Non-triviality: by axiom (C)(d) the trace of gamma([Spec(k)]) is 1, so no nonzero multiple of [Spec(k)] is homologically trivial.
Record that the relation is attached to H, and that the converse implication is Conjecture D (MC.7).
acceptance: The relation is a function of the chosen Weil cohomology theory and is written with it; an unqualified phrase homological equivalence is not well formed.
Homological triviality implies numerical triviality, with the proof passing through the degree computation of the layer above.
The converse implication is Conjecture D and is not available.

nodes.title: Chow motives over k
nodes.statement: A Chow motive over k is a triple (X, p, m) consisting of a smooth projective scheme X over k, an idempotent p in the degree zero correspondences from X to X, and an integer m. A morphism from (X, p, m) to (Y, q, n) is an element of the subgroup q o Corr^{n-m}(X, Y) o p of Corr^{n-m}(X, Y). Composition is the composition of correspondences. Equivalently, the category M_k of Chow motives is the Karoubi envelope of the category C_k of pairs (X, m) of MC.1/twisted-correspondence-category: the Karoubi object ((X, m), p) is the motive (X, p, m), and a Karoubi morphism, an element f of Corr^{n-m}(X, Y) with q o f o p = f, is exactly a morphism of motives.
hypotheses: X and Y are smooth projective schemes over k.
p and q are idempotent for the composition of correspondences.
m and n are integers; the convention is contravariant, so that the motive functor sends a morphism to the class of its graph.
proofSteps: Take the category C_k of pairs (X, m) with morphisms Corr^{n-m}(X, Y) (MC.1/twisted-correspondence-category).
Define the objects as triples and the morphism groups as the two-sided cut q o Corr^{n-m}(X, Y) o p.
Check that the cut is closed under composition and that degrees add: a morphism from (X, p, m) to (Y, q, n) followed by one to (Z, r, l) has degree (n - m) + (l - n) = l - m.
Check that p is the identity of (X, p, m).

Identify the result with Mathlib's Karoubi envelope of C_k: a Karoubi object is a pair of an object (X, m) and an idempotent p of degree zero, and Mathlib's Karoubi.Hom condition, p then f then q equals f in diagrammatic order, is q o f o p = f.
acceptance: Morphisms are cut on both sides: an element of the correspondences of degree n - m that is not fixed by q on the left and p on the right is not a morphism.
The degree of a morphism is n - m, so twisting shifts degrees and the identity of a twisted object is still p.
For p and q the identities and m = n = 0 the morphisms are the degree zero correspondences, so the category of correspondences embeds.

nodes.title: The motive of a smooth projective scheme
nodes.statement: There is a contravariant functor h from the category of smooth projective schemes over k to the category of motives, defined on objects by sending X to the triple (X, the class of the diagonal, 0) and on a morphism f by the class of its graph. It sends disjoint unions to direct sums and products to tensor products.
hypotheses: X is a smooth projective scheme over k and f a morphism of such.
proofSteps: Take the contravariant functor into correspondences (MC.0/correspondence-functor) and compose with the inclusion of the degree zero category into motives, X -> (X, [Delta_X], 0), which is the composite of X -> (X, 0) into C_k with Mathlib's toKaroubi.
Check that the graph of f, which has degree zero, is a morphism of motives between the corresponding triples, since it is fixed by both diagonals.
Functoriality is the functoriality of graphs.
Products go to tensor products: h(X × Y) and h(X) tensor h(Y) are the same triple, because the tensor product of the diagonals of X and Y is the diagonal of X × Y (MC.0/tensor-interchange).

Disjoint unions go to direct sums: the biproduct structure of X' coproduct X'' in the degree zero category (MC.0/correspondences-of-disjoint-union) is carried to motives by the fully faithful inclusion.
acceptance: The functor is contravariant, and h(X) has X as underlying scheme.
It sends the product of two schemes to the tensor product of their motives and a disjoint union to a direct sum.

h is not faithful: two distinct rational points x and y of P^1, viewed as morphisms Spec(k) -> P^1, have graphs [x] and [y] in CH^1(P^1) tensor Q, which are equal, so h(x) = h(y). The inclusion of the degree zero category of correspondences into motives is fully faithful but not essentially surjective, since a general motive carries a projector and a twist.

nodes.title: The category of motives is Karoubian
nodes.statement: Every idempotent endomorphism of a motive splits. Concretely, if a is an idempotent endomorphism of (X, p, m) then the triple (X, a, m) is a motive, a defines a morphism from it to (X, p, m), and this morphism is the kernel of the idempotent given by the identity minus a.
hypotheses: (X, p, m) is a motive and a an idempotent endomorphism of it.
proofSteps: Note that a is idempotent both as an endomorphism of the motive and as a correspondence, and a lies in Corr^0(X, X), so (X, a, m) is a motive.

Use a = p o a o a, which holds because a = a o a and a = p o a, to see that a lies in p o Corr^0(X, X) o a, so that a defines a morphism from (X, a, m) to (X, p, m); the same identity read as a = a o a o p shows that a is also a morphism from (X, p, m) to (X, a, m).
The two morphisms split the idempotent: their composite on (X, a, m) is a o a = a, its identity, and the composite on (X, p, m) is a.
Given b from (Y, q, n) to (X, p, m) with (p - a) o b = 0, deduce b = a o b and b = b o q, so that b factors, uniquely, through (X, a, m); so p - a has a kernel.
Through the identification of M_k with the Karoubi envelope of C_k this is Mathlib's instance that a Karoubi envelope is idempotent complete.
acceptance: Splitting is by the same scheme X with a different projector; the construction does not enlarge the class of underlying schemes.
The splitting is functorial in the sense required by the definition of a Karoubian category.
Applied to the two projectors on the projective line this splits h of the line into two summands.

sources.excerpt: The category M_k is Karoubian. Let M = (X, p, m) be a motive and let a be a projector in the endomorphisms of M. Set N = (X, a, m). Since we have a = p after a after a in Corr^0(X, X) we see that a : N to M is a morphism of M_k.

nodes.title: The tensor product of motives
nodes.statement: Define the tensor product of (X, p, m) and (Y, q, n) to be (X times Y, p tensor q, m + n), and the tensor product of morphisms by the tensor product of correspondences. With the associativity and commutativity constraints induced from products of schemes this makes the category of motives symmetric monoidal with unit the triple consisting of the spectrum of k, the identity and zero.
hypotheses: (X, p, m) and (Y, q, n) are motives and the morphisms are given in the two-sided cut form.
The tensor product of correspondences is the one constructed on the category of correspondences.
proofSteps: Check that the tensor product of two idempotent correspondences is idempotent, by the interchange law (MC.0/tensor-interchange), so the formula on objects gives a motive.

For morphisms, write each as q o c o p and use the interchange law to see that (q o c o p) tensor (q' o c' o p') = (q tensor q') o (c tensor c') o (p tensor p'), which is in cut form for the tensor product objects, as the source does.

Transport the associativity and commutativity constraints from correspondences; they are graphs of isomorphisms of schemes and are degree zero, so they are morphisms between the triples with the twists added.
Check the unit laws, and that the tensor product is Q-bilinear on morphisms, so that M_k is MonoidalPreadditive and MonoidalLinear over Q.
acceptance: The twist adds: the tensor product of an m-twist and an n-twist is an (m+n)-twist.
The unit is the motive of the spectrum of k.
The structure is symmetric, with the switch of factors as the constraint; this is the constraint Jannsen's corollary later modifies by a sign.

nodes.title: The Tate twist and the twisted unit motives
nodes.statement: For an integer n write 1(n) for the motive consisting of the spectrum of k, the identity and n. Then 1(0) is the unit, 1(n + m) is 1(n) tensor 1(m), and tensoring with 1(1) is an autoequivalence of the category of motives. For a motive M write M(n) for M tensor 1(n); if M is (X, p, m) then M(n) is (X, p, m + n).
hypotheses: n and m are integers and M is a motive.
proofSteps: Define 1(n) and check the two displayed identities from the definition of the tensor product.
Check that tensoring with 1(1) has tensoring with 1(-1) as an inverse up to natural isomorphism, so it is an autoequivalence.
Check the formula for M(n) on triples.
acceptance: Twisting only changes the third slot of the triple, so the underlying scheme and projector are unchanged.
Tensoring with 1(1) is invertible, which is what makes the category of motives, unlike the category of effective motives, closed under the twist.
1(0) is the unit.

sources.excerpt: The motives 1(n) = (Spec(k), 1, n) are useful. Observe that 1 = 1(0) and 1(n + m) = 1(n) tensor 1(m). Thus tensoring with 1(1) is an autoequivalence of the category of motives. Given a motive M we sometimes write M(n) = M tensor 1(n). Observe that if M = (X, p, m), then M(n) = (X, p, m + n).

nodes.title: The Lefschetz motive is the inverse Tate twist
nodes.statement: Let X be the projective line with the two orthogonal projectors c_0 and c_2 attached to a rational point. Then (X, c_0, 0) is isomorphic to the unit motive and (X, c_2, 0) is isomorphic to 1(-1). The second is the Lefschetz motive; it is invertible with inverse 1(1), the Tate motive.
hypotheses: X is the projective line over k with a chosen rational point x, and c_0 and c_2 are the two projectors.
proofSteps: For the first statement, let a be the correspondence attached to the structure morphism from X to the spectrum of k and b the one attached to the point x. Check that b after a is the identity of the point and that a after b is c_0, then check that a and b are morphisms between the two motives and are mutually inverse.

For the second statement, let a' be the class of the point x in the correspondences of degree one from the spectrum of k to X and b' the class of X in the correspondences of degree minus one from X to the spectrum of k. Compute that b' after a' is the identity of the point, using that the intersection of the class of x with the class of X is the class of x.
Compute the intersection product on X times the point times X to see that a' after b' is c_2.
Identify the morphism groups between 1(-1) and (X, c_2, 0) with the cut subgroups and conclude that a' and b' are mutually inverse morphisms.
Record the invertibility of the Lefschetz motive and the names in the literature.
acceptance: The isomorphism to 1(-1) is with the twist minus one and not plus one; the sign is fixed by the computation of a' after b'.
The Lefschetz motive is invertible for the tensor product, which is what makes the twist an autoequivalence.
The unit summand is the image of the projector of a point and the Lefschetz summand is the image of the complementary projector.

nodes.title: The category of motives is additive
nodes.statement: The category of motives is additive. For motives (Y, p, m) and (Z, q, m) with the same twist, (Y coproduct Z, p + q, m) is a biproduct, where p + q is the block diagonal correspondence on Y coproduct Z. If n < m, then (Z, q, n) is isomorphic to (Z × (P^1)^{m-n}, q tensor c_2 tensor ... tensor c_2, m) (MC.1/lower-twist-by-lefschetz), which reduces the general case to equal twists. The motive (empty scheme, 0, 0) is a zero object.
hypotheses: (Y, p, m) and (Z, q, n) are motives; without loss of generality n is at most m.
proofSteps: If m = n, the matrix description of correspondences between disjoint unions (MC.0/correspondences-of-disjoint-union) gives the inclusions and projections of the biproduct, cut by p and q.
If n < m, replace (Z, q, n) by the isomorphic motive of MC.1/lower-twist-by-lefschetz, whose twist is m.
Apply the equal-twist case, and take (empty scheme, 0, 0) as zero object; any (X, 0, m) is also a zero object.
acceptance: The direct sum of two motives with the same twist is again a motive on the disjoint union, with no new scheme introduced.
The reduction to equal twists uses the invertibility of the Lefschetz motive and nothing else.
With the zero motive, given by the empty scheme, this makes the category additive.

sources.excerpt: The category M_k is additive. [...] If n = m, then a direct sum is given by (Y coproduct Z, p + q, m), with obvious notation. Details omitted. Suppose that n < m. [...] This reduces us to the case discussed in the first paragraph.

nodes.title: The motive of the projective line
nodes.statement: In the category of motives, h of the projective line is isomorphic to the direct sum of the unit and 1(-1).
hypotheses: k is a field and the projective line carries a rational point, which it does over any field.
proofSteps: Split h of the line along the two orthogonal projectors, using that idempotents split.
Identify the two summands with the unit and 1(-1).
Assemble the two identifications into an isomorphism of motives.
acceptance: The decomposition has exactly two summands, one of which is a twist of the unit; a decomposition into two copies of the unit is wrong and is detected by any realisation, where the second summand sits in degree two.
The isomorphism depends on the chosen rational point only up to the identifications already made.
This is the first computation any implementation of motives should reproduce.

nodes.title: The universal property of the category of Chow motives
nodes.statement: Let C be a Q-linear Karoubian symmetric monoidal category, and let F be a Q-linear symmetric monoidal functor from the category whose objects are smooth projective schemes over k and whose morphisms are correspondences of degree zero to C, such that the image U of the projector F(c_2) on F(P^1_k) is an invertible object of C. Then there is a Q-linear symmetric monoidal functor G from the category of motives to C together with a monoidal natural isomorphism from G o i to F, where i sends X to h(X) = (X, [Delta], 0); and for any two such pairs there is a unique monoidal natural isomorphism between the functors compatible with the given isomorphisms.
hypotheses: C is Q-linear, Karoubian and symmetric monoidal.
F is a Q-linear symmetric monoidal functor from the degree zero correspondence category to C.
The image of c_2 in F of the projective line is invertible; without this the extension to twists does not exist.
proofSteps: On objects of degree zero twist, extend F through the Karoubi envelope: (X, p, 0) goes to the image of F(p), which exists because C is Karoubian; this is Mathlib's extension of functors to the Karoubi envelope (karoubiUniversal) applied to the degree zero part of C_k.
Put G(X, p, m) = (image of F(p)) tensor U^{tensor -m}, using that U is invertible, and check that G is compatible with tensor products on objects and that G(P^1_k, c_2, 0) = U.

On morphisms of equal twist use F directly. For a morphism a from (Y, p, m) to (Z, q, n) with n < m, compose with the isomorphism sigma : (Z, q, n) -> (Z × (P^1)^{m-n}, q tensor c_2^{tensor (m-n)}, m) of MC.1/lower-twist-by-lefschetz and with the matching isomorphism s on the side of C built from U = G(P^1, c_2, 0), and set G(a) = s^{-1} o F(sigma o a); for n > m use tau and t in the same way.
Check that the two recipes agree where both apply, and that G is a Q-linear symmetric monoidal functor; the source omits this verification.

Uniqueness: every motive is a summand of some h(X)(m). For m <= 0, h(X)(m) is isomorphic to a summand of h(X × (P^1)^{-m}) (MC.1/lower-twist-by-lefschetz); for m > 0, h(X)(m) is h(X) tensor an inverse of 1(-m), and a symmetric monoidal functor carries an inverse of an invertible object to an inverse, unique up to unique isomorphism. So a pair (G, iso) is determined up to unique monoidal isomorphism by its restriction along i.
acceptance: The hypothesis is invertibility of the image of c_2 and not of the image of the whole of h(P^1).
The extension is unique up to unique monoidal isomorphism compatible with the given isomorphism on the image of h.
Applied with C the category of graded vector spaces this is the construction of the functor attached to a Weil cohomology theory in MC.2.

sources.excerpt: Let C be a Q-linear Karoubian symmetric monoidal category. Any Q-linear functor F [...] to C of symmetric monoidal categories such that the image of F(c_2) on F(X) is an invertible object, factors uniquely through a functor F : M_k to C of symmetric monoidal categories.
sources.match: The node is that lemma; the source omits the verification that the extension is a symmetric monoidal functor ('We omit the verification'), so that verification is a proof step of this blueprint.

nodes.title: The motive of an equidimensional scheme is dualisable
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth projective scheme over k, equidimensional of dimension d. Then h(X) and h(X)(d) form an exact pairing: with coevaluation eta : 1 -> h(X) tensor h(X)(d) the class of the diagonal in Hom(1, h(X) tensor h(X)(d)) = Corr^d(Spec(k), X × X) = CH^d(X × X) tensor Q, and evaluation epsilon : h(X)(d) tensor h(X) -> 1 the class of the diagonal in Hom(h(X)(d) tensor h(X), 1) = Corr^{-d}(X × X, Spec(k)) = CH_d(X × X) tensor Q, both zig-zag identities hold. In the Stacks Project's terminology h(X)(d) is a left dual of h(X); in Mathlib's this is ExactPairing (h X) (h X (d)), so h(X)(d) is the right dual of h(X).
hypotheses: X is smooth projective over k and equidimensional of dimension d.
proofSteps: Compute Hom(1, h(X) tensor h(X)(d)) = Corr^d(Spec(k), X × X) = CH^d(X × X) tensor Q and Hom(h(X)(d) tensor h(X), 1) = Corr^{-d}(X × X, Spec(k)) = CH_d(X × X) tensor Q (MC.0/correspondences-with-the-point), and take the class of the diagonal in both.

Write eta tensor 1 in Corr^d(X, X × X × X) = CH^{2d}(X^4) as the class of pr_{23}^{-1}(Delta) cap pr_{14}^{-1}(Delta), and 1 tensor epsilon in Corr^{-d}(X × X × X, X) = CH^{2d}(X^4) as the class of the same cycle (MC.0/tensor-interchange for tensor products with the identity).

The composite (1 tensor epsilon) o (eta tensor 1) is the pushforward along pr_{15} of the product, on X^5, of pr_{23}^{-1}(Delta) cap pr_{14}^{-1}(Delta) and pr_{34}^{-1}(Delta) cap pr_{25}^{-1}(Delta); these meet properly in the small diagonal, which pushes forward to the diagonal of X, the identity. The source prints pr_{15} for pr_{25} in the second cycle (sourceIssues MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles/E8).
The other zig-zag, which the source omits, is the same computation with the roles of the factors exchanged.
acceptance: The dual of h(X) is the d-fold twist of h(X) and not h(X) itself; the twist is what makes the degrees match.
Both structure maps of the duality are the diagonal class, so the duality is canonical and does not depend on choices.
For X a point this is the statement that the unit is self dual.

sources.excerpt: Let X be a smooth projective scheme over k which is equidimensional of dimension d. Then h(X)(d) is a left dual to h(X) in M_k. [...] Here we have eta = [Delta]. [...] and here we have the class epsilon = [Delta] of the diagonal as well.
sources.match: The node is that lemma with its zig-zag computation on the fourfold and fivefold products; 'left dual' in the source's sense (Categories 0FFP) is an exact pairing (h(X), h(X)(d)) in Mathlib's sense.

nodes.title: Every Chow motive has a dual
nodes.statement: Every Chow motive M has a dual: there is a motive M' with an exact pairing (M, M') in Mathlib's sense (a left dual of M in the Stacks Project's sense). Hence the category of motives is right rigid in Mathlib's sense, and, being symmetric, rigid.
hypotheses: M is a motive.
proofSteps: Write M = (X, p, m) as a summand of h(X)(m) = (X, [Delta], m): the idempotent p of h(X)(m) splits with image M.
A summand of an object with a dual has a dual in a Karoubian category (MC.1/dual-of-summand), so it suffices to treat h(X)(m) = h(X) tensor 1(m).

1(-m) is a dual of 1(m), since 1(m) tensor 1(-m) = 1 = 1(-m) tensor 1(m) with identity coevaluation and evaluation; a tensor product of objects with duals has a dual (Mathlib's ExactPairing.tensor). So it suffices to treat h(X).

Decompose X into its connected components X_i, which for smooth X are its irreducible components and are equidimensional; then h(X) is the direct sum of the h(X_i) (MC.1/motive-functor-h, disjoint unions), and a direct sum of objects with duals has a dual (MC.1/dual-of-biproduct).
For each X_i apply MC.1/motive-dual.
Conclude RightRigidCategory, and RigidCategory by the symmetry (Mathlib's BraidedCategory.rigidCategoryOfRightRigidCategory).
acceptance: Rigidity holds for every motive, not only for motives of equidimensional schemes.
The dual of h(X) for X equidimensional of dimension d is h(X)(d), in the sense of an exact pairing (h(X), h(X)(d)).
The category is rigid on both sides: the left duals come from the right duals through the symmetry.

sources.excerpt: Every object of M_k has a left dual. [...] Then M is a summand of (X, 1, m) = h(X)(m). [...] By construction 1(-m) is a left dual of 1(m). Hence it suffices to show that h(X) has a left dual [...]. Then h(X) = direct sum of h(X_i)
sources.match: The node is that lemma with its reduction steps kept separate; each categorical input the source cites (Homology 0FFU, Categories 0FFS, Homology 0FFT) is a prerequisite.

nodes.title: Chow groups of a motive
nodes.statement: For a motive (X, p, m) and an integer i define the i-th Chow group of the motive as the image of the projector p acting on CH^{i+m}(X) tensor Q. For X smooth projective this gives back CH^i(X) tensor Q on h(X). A morphism of motives acts by pushforward of cycles, so each Chow group is a functor from motives to Q-vector spaces.
hypotheses: (X, p, m) is a motive and i an integer.
The action of p on cycles is the pushforward by the correspondence p.
proofSteps: Define the group as the image of the idempotent p acting on the twisted Chow group.
Check that for p the diagonal and m zero this is CH^i(X) tensor Q.

Check functoriality: a morphism c from (X, p, m) to (Y, q, n) is a correspondence of degree n - m, so pushforward by c maps CH^{i+m}(X) tensor Q to CH^{i+n}(Y) tensor Q, and the relation c = q after c after p makes it carry the image of p into the image of q.
Check compatibility with composition from the composition lemma.
acceptance: The index shift by m is part of the definition; dropping it makes the functor disagree with the twist.
On h(X) the functor returns the rational Chow groups of X.
The functor is Q-linear and additive in the motive.

sources.locator: Definition 0FGL and the paragraph after it
sources.excerpt: Let M = (X, p, m) be a Chow motive over k. For i in Z we define the i-th Chow group of M by the formula CH^i(M) = p(CH^{i+m}(X) tensor Q). We have CH^i(h(X)) = CH^i(X) tensor Q if X is a smooth projective scheme over k. Observe that CH^i(-) is a functor from M_k to Q-vector spaces.
sources.match: The node is that definition with the functoriality the source establishes in the following paragraph.

tests.name: chow_of_the_unit
tests.statement: CH^0 of the unit motive is Q and CH^i(1) = 0 for i nonzero.

tests.name: twist_shifts
tests.statement: CH^j(1(-i)) = CH^{j-i}(Spec(k)) tensor Q is Q for j = i and zero otherwise; a definition without the shift by m gives Q in degree zero for every i.

tests.name: projector_matters
tests.statement: For P^1 and the projector c_0 = [x × P^1], CH^0(P^1, c_0, 0) = Q and CH^1(P^1, c_0, 0) = 0, the Chow groups of a point; for c_2 = [P^1 × x] they are 0 and Q.

nodes.title: Chow groups of motives are representable
nodes.statement: For each integer i the functor sending a motive to its i-th Chow group is represented by 1(-i): there is an isomorphism, natural in the motive, between the i-th Chow group of M and the group of morphisms from 1(-i) to M.
hypotheses: M is a motive and i an integer.
proofSteps: Unfold the morphism group from 1(-i) to (X, p, m): it is the two-sided cut of the correspondences of degree m + i from the spectrum of k to X.
Identify the correspondences of degree m + i from the spectrum of k to X with CH^{m+i}(X) tensor Q.
Check that cutting by p on the left is exactly taking the image of the projector.
Check naturality in M, which is the compatibility of composition with pushforward of cycles.
acceptance: The representing object is 1(-i), with the sign as stated.
The isomorphism is natural, which is what makes it usable in the identity principle.
For i zero and M the unit the statement returns Q on both sides.

sources.excerpt: The functor CH^i(-) on the category of motives M_k is representable by 1(-i), that is, we have CH^i(M) = Hom_{M_k}(1(-i), M) functorially in M in M_k. Immediate from the definitions and Lemma 0FG0.
sources.match: The node is that lemma, with the unfolding the source calls immediate written out as four proof steps.

nodes.title: Manin's identity principle
nodes.statement: Let c be a morphism of motives from M to N. If for every smooth projective scheme X over k the morphism c tensor the identity of h(X) induces an isomorphism on all Chow groups, then c is an isomorphism.
hypotheses: c is a morphism of motives and the hypothesis is quantified over all smooth projective X over k.
proofSteps: Every motive L is a summand of a twist h(X)(m), and the Chow groups of M tensor h(X)(m) are those of M tensor h(X) shifted by m (the twist API of the Chow group node); since Chow groups are additive, the hypothesis holds with h(X) replaced by any motive L.
By representability, CH^i(M tensor L) = Hom(1(-i), M tensor L) = Hom(1, M tensor L(i)), so Hom(1, M tensor L) -> Hom(1, N tensor L) is bijective for every L.

For any motive K with dual K' (an exact pairing (K, K')), Mathlib's tensorRightHomEquiv identifies Hom(1 tensor K, M) with Hom(1, M tensor K') naturally in M, so Hom(K, M) -> Hom(K, N) is bijective for every K.
Conclude by the Yoneda lemma in the form isIso_of_yoneda_map_bijective.
acceptance: The hypothesis must be tested after tensoring with every smooth projective X; testing only on the Chow groups of M and N is not enough.
The conclusion is that c is an isomorphism of motives, not only that it induces isomorphisms on Chow groups.
The proof uses rigidity, so it does not transfer to a setting where duals are missing.

sources.excerpt: Let c : M to N be a morphism of motives. If for every smooth projective scheme X over k the map c tensor 1 : M tensor h(X) to N tensor h(X) induces an isomorphism on Chow groups, then c is an isomorphism.
sources.match: The node is that lemma, attributed to Manin in the source, with its four proof steps kept separate; the third uses that every object has a left dual, which is why rigidity is a prerequisite.

nodes.title: The projective bundle formula for motives
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth projective scheme over k and E a locally free module of rank r on X, with P the associated projective bundle and p its structure morphism, normalised so that the pushforward of the twisting sheaf of degree one is E. For i from 0 to r - 1 let c_i be the correspondence obtained by capping the class of the graph of p with the i-th power of the first Chern class of the pullback of the twisting sheaf along the second projection, viewed as a morphism from h(X)(-i) to h(P). Then the sum of the c_i is an isomorphism from the direct sum of the h(X)(-i) to h(P).
hypotheses: X is smooth projective over k and E is locally free of rank r.
The projective bundle is the Proj of the symmetric algebra of E, with the normalisation of the twisting sheaf stated.
The Chern class used is that of the pullback of the twisting sheaf along the second projection.
proofSteps: Define the correspondences c_i = c_1(pr_2^*O_P(1))^i cap [Gamma_p] in Corr^i(X, P) and check that each has degree i, so that it is a morphism from h(X)(-i) to h(P).
Apply the identity principle: it suffices to show that the sum induces isomorphisms on Chow groups after tensoring with h(Z) for an arbitrary smooth projective Z.

Identify c_i tensor 1_{h(Z)} with the correspondence c_i built for P × Z -> X × Z: the tensor product of the graphs of p and of the identity of Z is the graph of p × id (MC.0/tensor-interchange), capping with Chern classes commutes with exterior products, and O_{P × Z}(1) is the pullback of O_P(1). P × Z -> X × Z is the projective bundle of the pullback of E.

Pushforward along c_i sends alpha to c_1(O_P(1))^i cap p^*alpha, since pushforward along [Gamma_p] is the Gysin map p^!, which is flat pullback for the flat p (MC.0/graph-acts-as-gysin-and-pushforward; Stacks 0FF4).

The Chow groups of the direct sum of the h(X × Z)(-i) are the direct sum of the shifted Chow groups of X × Z, and the induced map is the map of the projective bundle formula for Chow groups (Stacks 02TX, imported from SF.5), which is an isomorphism.
acceptance: The summands are twists h(X)(-i) for i from 0 to r - 1; a formula with r summands untwisted is wrong and fails already for the projective line.
The isomorphism is given by the explicit correspondences c_i and not merely asserted to exist.
For E free of rank two over the spectrum of k this recovers the decomposition of the motive of the projective line.

sources.locator: Lemma 0FGQ with its proof, and the paragraph of Section 0FGP defining the correspondences c_i
sources.excerpt: the map sum over i = 0, ..., r - 1 of c_i : direct sum of h(X)(-i) to h(P) is an isomorphism in the category of motives. [...] By Lemma 0FGN it suffices to show that our map defines an isomorphism on Chow groups of motives after taking the product with any smooth projective scheme Z.
sources.match: The node is that lemma with the definition of the c_i from the preceding paragraph, including the normalisation p_*(O_P(1)) = E, which the source fixes explicitly.

nodes.title: The class of the diagonal of a projective bundle
nodes.statement: With the notation of the projective bundle formula, let S be the kernel of the canonical surjection p^*E -> O_P(1), locally free of rank r - 1. Then the class of the diagonal of P in CH^*(P × P) is [Delta_P] = (sum over i from 0 to r - 1 of c_{r-1-i}(pr_1^*S^dual) . c_1(pr_2^*O_P(1))^i) cap (p × p)^*[Delta_X]. Every coefficient is 1. The source prints binomial coefficients (r - 1 choose i), which is wrong for r >= 3 (sourceIssues MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles/E9).
hypotheses: The setting is that of the projective bundle formula: X smooth projective over k, E locally free of rank r, P = P(E) with p_*O_P(1) = E.
S is the kernel of the canonical surjection p^*E -> O_P(1), locally free of rank r - 1.
proofSteps: Reduce to the fibre product P ×_X P: (p × p)^*[Delta_X] = [P ×_X P], Delta_P lies in P ×_X P, and capping with Chern classes commutes with proper pushforward (Stacks 02U9).

The diagonal of P is the zero scheme of the section of q_1^*S^dual tensor q_2^*O_P(1) built from the evaluation pairing, and [Delta_P] = c_{r-1}(q_1^*S^dual tensor q_2^*O_P(1)) cap [P ×_X P] (MC.1/diagonal-as-zero-scheme).

Expand the top Chern class of a rank r - 1 bundle twisted by a line bundle by Stacks 02UD: c_{r-1}(V tensor L) = sum over j of binom(j, j) c_{r-1-j}(V) c_1(L)^j = sum over j of c_{r-1-j}(V) c_1(L)^j, which is the displayed formula with all coefficients 1.
acceptance: All coefficients are 1; the printed binomial coefficients fail for r = 3: over Spec(k), P = P^2 and [Delta] . (h_1 h_2) must be 1 (the diagonal meets L × L' in one point), and the printed formula gives 2.
A formula without the dual of S fails already for r = 2: for P^1 it would give -h_1 + h_2.
For r = 1 the bundle is X and the formula returns the diagonal of X; for X = Spec(k) and E of rank n + 1 it returns [Delta_{P^n}] = sum over i of h_1^{n-i} h_2^i.

sources.excerpt: The class of the diagonal of P in CH^*(P times P) can be written as the cap of the sum over i of (r - 1 choose i) c_{r-1-i}(pr_1^* S dual) with c_1(pr_2^* O_P(1))^i, applied to (p times p)^*[Delta_X], where S is the kernel of the canonical surjection p^* E to O_P(1).
sources.match: The node is that lemma with the coefficients corrected to 1 (sourceIssues MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles/E9): the source's proof ends by citing Stacks 02UD, whose top-degree case has all coefficients binom(j, j) = 1.

nodes.title: Motives modulo an arbitrary adequate equivalence relation
nodes.statement: Fix a field F of characteristic zero and an adequate family I (MC.0/adequate-equivalence-relation). Form correspondences modulo I, Corr_I^r(X, Y) = direct sum over d of A^{d+r}(X_d × Y, F), with the composition and tensor product induced from those of Chow correspondences, and the category M_k(I) of triples (X, p, m) with p an idempotent of Corr_I^0(X, X) and morphisms q o Corr_I^{n-m}(X, Y) o p. The result is an F-linear, pseudo-abelian, symmetric monoidal category with unit (Spec(k), id, 0) and tensor product (X, p, m) tensor (Y, q, n) = (X × Y, p tensor q, m + n); it is rigid, the internal Hom from (X, p, m) to (Y, q, n) for X irreducible being (X × Y, p^t tensor q, dim X - m + n). For I = 0 and F = Q it is the category of Chow motives; for the trivial relation it is the zero category.
hypotheses: F is a field of characteristic zero and the relation is adequate.
Varieties are smooth projective over k.
The rigidity statement is for the internal hom formula as displayed, and the formula is stated for irreducible X.
proofSteps: Correspondences modulo I and their composition and tensor product descend from Chow correspondences tensor F, because I is stable under pullback, products and pushforward (MC.0/adequate-equivalence-relation).

Equivalently, the category of pairs (X, m) with morphisms Corr_I^{n-m}(X, Y) is the quotient of C_k tensor F by the ideal of morphisms with classes in I (Mathlib's Quotient category with its preadditive and linear structures), and M_k(I) is its Karoubi envelope; in particular it is pseudo-abelian.
The tensor structure and its constraints descend from those of Chow motives, by MC.1/motives-monoidal.

Rigidity: the proof of MC.1/motives-rigid goes through modulo I (the zig-zag identities are identities of correspondences, which descend), and the internal Hom is the dual of (X, p, m) tensored with (Y, q, n), the dual of (X, p, m) for X irreducible being (X, p^t, dim X - m).
For I = 0 and F = Q nothing changes; for the trivial relation all morphism groups vanish.
acceptance: The construction is parametrised by the relation and by F; nothing identifies two different choices.
Taking rational equivalence returns the category of Chow motives.
The internal hom formula shows rigidity for every adequate relation, so rigidity is not what distinguishes numerical equivalence.

sources.locator: page 448, the sentence after the Remark, and page 450, the proof of Corollary 2
sources.excerpt: M_k is an F-linear, pseudo-abelian category, cf. [K2] Sect. 5. [...] Moreover, M_k is rigid ([DM] 1.7), with the internal Hom in the case of an irreducible X defined by Hom((X, p, m), (Y, q, n)) = (X times Y, ^tp times q, dim(X) - m + n).
sources.match: The node is that construction, taken from the two places in the source where it is set up and then recalled with its tensor structure and internal Hom.

nodes.title: The data of a Weil cohomology theory
nodes.statement: Fix an algebraically closed field k and a field F of characteristic zero. The data of a Weil cohomology theory over k with coefficients in F consists of (D1) a contravariant functor from smooth projective varieties over k to graded commutative F-algebras, written X to H^*(X), whose value on a morphism f is the pullback f^*; graded commutative means a ∪ b = (−1)^{ij} b ∪ a for a in H^i(X) and b in H^j(X), the sign of the commutativity constraint of MC.2/graded-vector-spaces-koszul; (D2) for every smooth projective variety X and every integer i a group homomorphism γ from CH^i(X) to H^{2i}(X), the cycle class map; and (D3) for every smooth projective variety X of dimension d a map ∫_X from H^{2d}(X) to F, the trace map.
hypotheses: k is algebraically closed and F has characteristic zero; both hypotheses are used by the axioms and neither may be dropped silently.
Variety means a variety over k in the sense of the source, so in particular irreducible and of a well defined dimension.
The cycle class map is defined on the integral Chow groups CH^i(X) of SF.5 and doubles the degree.
The trace map is taken F-linear; the source calls it a map, and axioms (A)(b) and (A)(d) presuppose linearity.
Graded commutativity carries the Koszul sign (−1)^{ij}; a commutative graded algebra in the naive sense is a different notion.
proofSteps: Record the three pieces of data with their exact types, including that the target of (D1) is graded commutative F-algebras and not merely graded F-vector spaces.
Record that the cycle class map doubles degrees and that the trace map is defined on the top degree only, which is where the dimension of X enters.

Record the ambiguity the source flags: for a closed subscheme of a smooth projective subvariety of X the notation for the cycle class is ambiguous between the two ambient varieties, so every use names the ambient variety.
acceptance: The data alone is not a Weil cohomology theory; the axioms are separate and are stated in the next node.
The functor is contravariant and lands in algebras, so cup products are part of the data and not an extra structure.
The trace map depends on the dimension of X.

sources.locator: Section 0FGS, the list of data (D1), (D2), (D3) with the remarks following it
sources.excerpt: The data is given by: (D1) A contravariant functor H^* from the category of smooth projective varieties to the category of graded commutative F-algebras. (D2) For every smooth projective variety X a group homomorphism gamma from CH^i(X) to H^{2i}(X). (D3) For every smooth projective variety X of dimension d a map the integral over X from H^{2d}(X) to F.
sources.match: The node is that list together with the source's remarks naming pullback, the cycle class map and the trace map, and flagging the ambiguity of the cycle class notation.
