nodes.title: The register of known cases of the Hodge and Tate conjectures
nodes.statement: A register of what is proved, each entry with base field, characteristic, codimension, coefficients and premises; every entry is an instance of a predicate of this layer with its arguments fixed. Hodge conjecture: (H1) degree two (p = 1) for every projective non-singular X over C, characteristic zero, with integral and hence rational coefficients: a class in H^2(X, Z) of type (1, 1) is the first Chern class of a line bundle (Kodaira and Spencer, through the exponential sequence; the Lefschetz (1, 1) theorem). Tate conjecture, all with Q_l coefficients, l invertible in k, and codimension one: (T1) abelian varieties over a finite field (Tate), with the equivalent form that Hom_k(A, B) ⊗ Z_l → Hom_Gal(H_1(A, Z_l), H_1(B, Z_l)) is bijective for abelian varieties A, B over a finite field k, proved through Zarhin's trick (the principal polarisation of (A × Â)^4) and the finiteness of abelian varieties of bounded dimension over a finite field; the proof gives the strong Tate conjecture; (T2) abelian varieties over a number field (Faltings; FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems:R28.4 owns the isogeny theorem); (T3) abelian varieties over any finitely generated field (Zarhin, from Tate and Faltings); (T4) varieties over a number field with h^{2,0} = 0, by the Lefschetz (1, 1) theorem; (T5) K3 surfaces over number fields (Tankeev); (T6) irreducible hyperkähler varieties over number fields (André); (T7) smooth proper varieties with h^{2,0} = 1 over a finitely generated field of characteristic zero admitting an embedding of the field into C for which X_C has a deformation over a smooth base variety in which the Hodge structure on H^2(X_C, Q) varies nontrivially (Moonen, Theorem 4.1); (T8) K3 surfaces over finite fields: with an elliptic fibration (Artin and Swinnerton-Dyer), of degree 2 (Rudakov, Shafarevich and Zink), non-supersingular in characteristic p > 5 (Nygaard and Ogus), and supersingular (Charles, Maulik, Madapusi Pera, and Kim and Madapusi Pera, characteristic 2 only in the last), which the source calls the complete proof for K3 surfaces over finite fields. Beilinson's injectivity: (TB1) codimension one over a finite field, from the finiteness of the rational points of abelian varieties over finite fields. The source also reports cases for Hilbert and Picard modular surfaces and for some Shimura varieties without their hypotheses; these are not admissible entries until the hypotheses are obtained.
hypotheses: Every entry names its base field, characteristic, codimension and coefficients, and any finiteness premise; an entry without them is not admissible.
Every entry is recorded from the survey or the problem description; the primary proofs were not obtained (gaps), and the stage allows proving a case only after its primary proof is acquired.
A conjectural target never supplies an unconditional downstream theorem.
proofSteps: Record the Hodge entry H1 with Deligne's sketch: the image of a (1, 1) class in H^{0,2} = H^2(X, O) vanishes, and the exponential sequence makes it a first Chern class; the identification of H^{0,2} with H^2(X, O) uses the Hodge decomposition (gap).
Record T1 with its equivalent form and the structure of the proof from Totaro, Section 3, and that it gives the strong form.

Record T2 as a consequence of the isogeny theorem of R28.4 through NS(A × B) = NS(A) ⊕ NS(B) ⊕ Hom_k(A, B̂), which the source states for abelian varieties over any field, and T3 as Zarhin's extension.
Record T4 to T7 with their hypotheses, noting that the Kuga-Satake correspondence is not known to be algebraic and is used only through its effect on Hodge and Tate classes.
Record the K3 entries T8 with their characteristic restrictions and TB1 with its reason.
Record the unhypothesised reports (modular surfaces, Shimura varieties) as not admissible.
acceptance: Every entry is an instance of a predicate of this layer with its arguments fixed; nothing in the register is a general theorem.
The K3 entries over finite fields and the K3 entry over number fields are separate, with different proofs.
An entry whose hypotheses are not fully recorded is not admissible; the unhypothesised reports are listed as such.

nodes.title: Correspondences to and from the point are Chow groups
nodes.statement: For a smooth projective scheme X over k and an integer r there are canonical Q-linear isomorphisms CH_{-r}(X) tensor Q = Corr^r(X, Spec(k)) and CH^r(X) tensor Q = Corr^r(Spec(k), X), induced by X × Spec(k) = X = Spec(k) × X. Under the first, pullback of cycles by a correspondence c in Corr^s(W, X) is composition with c: c^*(beta) corresponds to beta o c. Under the second, pushforward of cycles by c in Corr^s(X, W) is composition: c_*(alpha) corresponds to c o alpha.
hypotheses: X and W are smooth projective over k; r and s are integers.
Cycle classes are rational.
proofSteps: On X_d, codimension d + r is dimension -r, so Corr^r(X, Spec(k)) = direct sum over d of CH^{d+r}(X_d) tensor Q = CH_{-r}(X) tensor Q; and Corr^r(Spec(k), X) = CH^{0+r}(X) tensor Q, since Spec(k) has dimension zero.

For beta in CH_{-r}(X) and c in Corr^s(W, X), beta o c = pr_{13,*}(pr_{12}^*c . pr_{23}^*beta) on W × X × Spec(k) = W × X, where pr_13 and pr_23 become pr_1 and pr_2; this is the defining formula of c^*(beta), in CH_{-r-s}(W).

For alpha in CH^r(X) and c in Corr^s(X, W), c o alpha = pr_{13,*}(pr_{12}^*alpha . pr_{23}^*c) on Spec(k) × X × W = X × W, which is pr_{2,*}(pr_1^*alpha . c) = c_*(alpha) by commutativity of the intersection product.
acceptance: The degrees match: beta o c has degree r + s and c^*(beta) has dimension -r - s.
For X = Spec(k) both isomorphisms identify Corr^0(Spec(k), Spec(k)) with Q and all other degrees with zero.
The class [X] in CH^0(X) corresponds to the graph of the structure morphism X -> Spec(k), a correspondence of degree zero from Spec(k) to X.

sources.excerpt: (2) there is a canonical isomorphism CH_{-r}(X) tensor Q = Corr^r(X, Spec(k)) such that pullback by correspondences corresponds to composition, (3) there is a canonical isomorphism CH^r(X) tensor Q = Corr^r(Spec(k), X) such that pushforward by correspondences corresponds to composition,

nodes.title: Composition of correspondences computes the action on cycles
nodes.statement: For c in Corr^r(X, Y) and c' in Corr^s(Y, Z) one has (c' o c)^*(beta) = c^*((c')^*(beta)) for beta in CH_*(Z) tensor Q and (c' o c)_*(alpha) = (c')_*(c_*(alpha)) for alpha in CH^*(X) tensor Q.

Cycle classes are rational.
proofSteps: Under the identifications of MC.0/correspondences-with-the-point, (c' o c)^*(beta) corresponds to beta o (c' o c) and c^*((c')^*(beta)) to (beta o c') o c; they agree by associativity.
Likewise (c' o c)_*(alpha) corresponds to (c' o c) o alpha and (c')_*(c_*(alpha)) to c' o (c o alpha).
acceptance: Pullback is contravariant and pushforward covariant in the correspondence.
For c' the diagonal both identities are trivial.
The identities hold in every degree, not only in degree zero.

nodes.title: Correspondences between disjoint unions, and additivity of the degree zero category
nodes.statement: Let X = X' coproduct X'' and Y = Y' coproduct Y'' be decompositions of smooth projective schemes over k into open and closed subschemes. Restriction gives a Q-linear isomorphism of Corr^r(X, Y) with the direct sum of Corr^r(X', Y'), Corr^r(X', Y''), Corr^r(X'', Y') and Corr^r(X'', Y''), under which composition of correspondences is multiplication of 2 × 2 matrices. In particular X is a biproduct of X' and X'' in the degree zero category of correspondences, the projections being the graphs of the inclusions and the injections the classes of the diagonals of X' and X'' viewed in X' × X and X'' × X, and the empty scheme is a zero object; the degree zero category is additive.
hypotheses: X' and X'' (and Y', Y'') are open and closed in X (and Y); either may be empty.
Cycle classes are rational.
proofSteps: The Chow groups of a disjoint union are the direct sum of those of the pieces (SF.5), (X' coproduct X'') × Y = (X' × Y) coproduct (X'' × Y), and the equidimensional decomposition of X is the union of those of X' and X'', so the degree shift is compatible.

Composition is matrix multiplication: in pr_{13,*}(pr_{12}^*c . pr_{23}^*c'), classes supported on X × Y' and on Y'' × Z pull back to classes supported on disjoint open and closed subschemes of X × Y × Z, whose product is zero.

Biproduct identities: projection to X' after injection of X' is [Delta_{X'}], projection to X' after injection of X'' is zero, and the sum of the two composites injection after projection is [Delta_X], from the matrix description and the fact that the diagonal is the identity.
Corr^r(empty, Y) and Corr^r(Y, empty) are zero.
acceptance: The matrix description holds in every degree r, not only in degree zero.
For X' = X and X'' empty the lemma is trivial.
h of a disjoint union is the direct sum of the h of the pieces, which is the property MC.1 uses.

nodes.title: The interchange law for the tensor product of correspondences
nodes.statement: For c in Corr^r(X, Y), d in Corr^s(Y, Z), c' in Corr^{r'}(X', Y') and d' in Corr^{s'}(Y', Z') one has (d tensor d') o (c tensor c') = (d o c) tensor (d' o c') in Corr^{r+s+r'+s'}(X × X', Z × Z'). The tensor product of the diagonals of X and X' is the diagonal of X × X', and the tensor product of the graphs of f : Y -> X and f' : Y' -> X' is the graph of f × f', and likewise for transposed graphs.
hypotheses: All schemes are smooth projective over k.
Cycle classes are rational.
proofSteps: Identify c tensor c' = pr_{13}^*c . pr_{24}^*c' with the exterior product c × c' transported along the isomorphism X × X' × Y × Y' = (X × Y) × (X' × Y').

On (X × Y × Z) × (X' × Y' × Z'), use that exterior products commute with flat pullback, that (a × a') . (b × b') = (a . b) × (a' . b'), and that (g × g')_*(a × a') = g_*a × g'_*a' for proper g, g' (SF.5), to identify both sides.

For graphs, Gamma_f × Gamma_{f'} = Gamma_{f × f'} as subschemes, isomorphic to the smooth Y × Y', so the exterior product of their classes is the class of the graph of f × f'; the diagonal case is f and f' identities, and transposed graphs are the same subschemes read in the switched product.
acceptance: The degrees add: (r + s) + (r' + s').
Taking d and d' diagonals recovers c tensor c', so the law is consistent with the identities.
On P^1 × P^1 with the projectors c_0, c_2: (c_0 tensor c_2) o (c_0 tensor c_2) = c_0 tensor c_2.

nodes.title: The graph of a morphism against the diagonals
nodes.statement: Let f : Y -> X be a morphism of smooth projective schemes over k, with X and Y equidimensional of dimensions d and e. Put a = [Gamma_f] in Corr^0(X, Y), a^t = [Gamma_f^t] in Corr^{d-e}(Y, X), eta_X in Corr^0(X × X, X) and eta_Y in Corr^0(Y × Y, Y) the graphs of the diagonal morphisms, and [X] in Corr^{-d}(X, Spec(k)), [Y] in Corr^{-e}(Y, Spec(k)) the fundamental classes. Then [Y] o eta_Y o (a tensor id_Y) = [X] o eta_X o (id_X tensor a^t) in Corr^{-e}(X × Y, Spec(k)) = CH^d(X × Y) tensor Q, and both equal the class of Gamma_f.
hypotheses: X and Y are equidimensional of dimensions d and e.
Cycle classes are rational.
proofSteps: By MC.0/correspondences-with-the-point, Corr^{-e}(X × Y, Spec(k)) = CH_e(X × Y) tensor Q and composition with a correspondence is pullback by it.

One way round: eta_Y^*[Y] = [Delta_Y] (pullback by the graph of the diagonal is pushforward along the diagonal, MC.0/graph-acts-as-gysin-and-pushforward), and a tensor id_Y is the graph of f × id_Y (MC.0/tensor-interchange), whose pullback is (f × id)_*, giving (f × id)_*[Delta_Y] = [Gamma_f].

Other way round: eta_X^*[X] = [Delta_X], id_X tensor a^t is the transposed graph of id × f, whose pullback is the Gysin map (id × f)^!, and (id × f)^![Delta_X] = [Gamma_f] because (id × f)^{-1}(Delta_X) = Gamma_f with the expected codimension (Stacks 0FF7).
The source writes the common value as an element of Corr^d(X × Y, Spec(k)); the degree is -e (sourceIssues MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles/E11).
acceptance: Both composites have degree -e, the degree of a cycle of dimension e on X × Y.
For f the identity of X both sides are the class of the diagonal.
The equality is of correspondences, not only of their actions on cycles.

nodes.title: The category of correspondences with twists
nodes.statement: Let C_k be the Q-linear category whose objects are pairs (X, m) of a smooth projective scheme X over k and an integer m, whose morphisms from (X, m) to (Y, n) are the correspondences Corr^{n-m}(X, Y), whose composition is composition of correspondences, and whose identities are the diagonal classes. The full subcategory on the objects (X, 0) is the degree zero category of correspondences.
hypotheses: X and Y are smooth projective over k; m and n are integers.
Cycle classes are rational.
proofSteps: Composition is well typed: a morphism (X, m) -> (Y, n) of degree n - m followed by one (Y, n) -> (Z, l) of degree l - n has degree l - m.
Associativity, bilinearity and the identity axiom are those of the graded category of correspondences (MC.0/composition-associative, MC.0/category-of-correspondences).
The shift (X, m) -> (X, m + 1), the identity on morphisms, is an automorphism of C_k.
acceptance: Morphisms between different twists are correspondences of nonzero degree.
The shift is an automorphism, not merely an equivalence.
The degree zero category embeds fully faithfully as the objects (X, 0).

nodes.title: Raising the twist by tensoring with the Lefschetz motive
nodes.statement: Let c_2 be the projector of Example 0FG6 on P^1_k. For a motive (Z, q, n) and an integer m >= n there is an isomorphism sigma from (Z, q, n) to (Z × (P^1)^{m-n}, q tensor c_2 tensor ... tensor c_2, m), namely the identity of (Z, q, m) tensored with m - n copies of the isomorphism a' : 1(-1) -> (P^1, c_2, 0) of MC.1/lefschetz-motive, composed with the identifications (Z, q, n) = (Z, q, m) tensor 1(-1)^{tensor (m-n)} and (Z, q, m) tensor (P^1, c_2, 0)^{tensor (m-n)} = (Z × (P^1)^{m-n}, q tensor c_2^{tensor (m-n)}, m).
hypotheses: (Z, q, n) is a motive and m >= n.
k is a field; P^1_k has the rational point used to define c_2.
proofSteps: (Z, q, m) tensor 1(-1)^{tensor (m-n)} is (Z × Spec(k)^{m-n}, q, n), which is (Z, q, n) through Z × Spec(k) = Z.
Tensor the identity of (Z, q, m) with (m - n) copies of a' and use functoriality of the tensor product of motives.
(Z, q, m) tensor (P^1, c_2, 0)^{tensor (m-n)} is the triple of the statement by the definition of the tensor product of motives.
acceptance: For m = n, sigma is the identity.
The twist is raised, not lowered: the target has twist m >= n.
sigma is an isomorphism of motives with inverse built from b'.

sources.excerpt: Suppose that n < m. Let X, c_2 be as in Example 0FG6. Then we consider (Z, q, n) = (Z, q, m) tensor (Spec(k), 1, -1) tensor ... tensor (Spec(k), 1, -1) =~ (Z, q, m) tensor (X, c_2, 0) tensor ... tensor (X, c_2, 0) =~ (Z × X^{m-n}, q tensor c_2 tensor ... tensor c_2, m)
sources.match: The node is that chain of isomorphisms, which the proof of Lemma 0FGH reuses as sigma.

nodes.title: A direct sum of objects with duals has a dual
nodes.statement: Let A be a preadditive monoidal category in which the tensor product is additive in each variable (Mathlib's MonoidalPreadditive). If (X_1, Y_1) and (X_2, Y_2) are exact pairings (coevaluation 1 -> X_i tensor Y_i, evaluation Y_i tensor X_i -> 1) and the biproducts X_1 + X_2 and Y_1 + Y_2 exist, then (X_1 + X_2, Y_1 + Y_2) is an exact pairing, with coevaluation the sum over i of (iota_i tensor iota_i) o eta_i and evaluation the sum over i of epsilon_i o (pi_i tensor pi_i). In the Stacks Project's terminology, Y_1 + Y_2 is a left dual of X_1 + X_2.
hypotheses: A is preadditive and monoidal with the tensor product additive in each variable.
The biproducts exist; the exact pairings are in Mathlib's convention.
proofSteps: Define the coevaluation and evaluation as in the statement.

Expand each zig-zag composite by additivity of the tensor product in each variable; the cross terms contain pi_j o iota_i = 0 for i different from j, and the diagonal terms are iota_i o (zig-zag for (X_i, Y_i)) o pi_i = iota_i o pi_i.
Sum the diagonal terms: iota_1 o pi_1 + iota_2 o pi_2 is the identity of the biproduct.
acceptance: The formulas use the biproduct structure maps on both sides.
For X_2 = Y_2 = 0 the pairing is (X_1, Y_1).
Applied in the category of motives, the dual of h(X' coproduct X'') is the direct sum of the duals of h(X') and h(X'').

sources.excerpt: Let A be an additive monoidal category. If Y_i, i = 1, 2 are left duals of X_i, i = 1, 2, then Y_1 ⊕ Y_2 is a left dual of X_1 ⊕ X_2. Proof. Follows from uniqueness of adjoints and Categories, Remark [left-dual-adjoint].
sources.match: The node is that lemma in Mathlib's convention; the proof steps are a direct computation in place of the source's appeal to uniqueness of adjoints. Cited by the proof of Lemma 0FGJ.

nodes.title: A summand of an object with a dual has a dual
nodes.statement: Let A be an idempotent complete (Karoubian) preadditive monoidal category. If (X, Y) is an exact pairing in Mathlib's convention and X' is a retract of X, with i : X' -> X and r : X -> X' such that r o i = id, then X' has a right dual: the idempotent e = i o r of X has an adjoint mate e^vee on Y, which is idempotent, and its image Y' with the restricted coevaluation and evaluation forms an exact pairing (X', Y'). In the Stacks Project's terminology, every summand of an object with a left dual has a left dual.
hypotheses: A is preadditive, monoidal and idempotent complete.
(X, Y) is an exact pairing; X' is a retract of X.
proofSteps: The adjoint mate (Mathlib's rightAdjointMate) is contravariantly functorial, so the mate of e = i o r is an idempotent e^vee of Y; split it as Y' with maps i' : Y' -> Y and r' : Y -> Y', r' o i' = id, i' o r' = e^vee.
Put eta' = (r tensor r') o eta and epsilon' = epsilon o (i' tensor i).
Check the two zig-zag identities for (eta', epsilon') from those for (eta, epsilon), using the mate identity (e tensor id) o eta = (id tensor e^vee) o eta and its counterpart for epsilon.
acceptance: The dual of X' is a summand of the dual of X.
For X' = X and i = r = id, (X', Y') is (X, Y).
Applied to motives, the dual of (X, p, m) is a summand of the dual of h(X)(m).

sources.excerpt: In a Karoubian additive monoidal category every summand of an object which has a left dual has a left dual. [...] If a : X → X corresponds to b : Y → Y then b is the unique endomorphism of Y such that precomposing by a [...] is the same as postcomposing by 1 ⊗ b.
sources.match: The node is that lemma in Mathlib's convention; the endomorphism b of the source is the adjoint mate. Cited by the proof of Lemma 0FGJ.

nodes.title: Explicit projectors on projective space
nodes.statement: Let n >= 0, P = P^n_k and h in CH^1(P) the class of a hyperplane. For i = 0, ..., n let c_i = h^i in Corr^i(Spec(k), P) = CH^i(P) tensor Q, a morphism 1(-i) -> h(P), and c'_i = h^{n-i} in Corr^{-i}(P, Spec(k)) = CH^{n-i}(P) tensor Q, a morphism h(P) -> 1(-i). Then c'_j o c_i is the identity for i = j and zero otherwise; the classes pi_i = c_i o c'_i = pr_1^*h^{n-i} . pr_2^*h^i in Corr^0(P, P) = CH^n(P × P) tensor Q are orthogonal idempotents with pi_0 + ... + pi_n = [Delta_P]; (P, pi_i, 0) is isomorphic to 1(-i); and h(P^n) is isomorphic to the direct sum of the 1(-i) for i = 0, ..., n. For n = 1 and a rational point x, pi_0 = [x × P^1] = c_0 and pi_1 = [P^1 × x] = c_2.
hypotheses: k is a field and n >= 0.
P^n_k = P(O^{n+1}) with the convention of the projective bundle formula, so that h = c_1(O(1)).
proofSteps: Identify Corr^i(Spec(k), P) with CH^i(P) and Corr^{-i}(P, Spec(k)) with CH^{n-i}(P) (MC.0/correspondences-with-the-point), and CH^*(P) tensor Q with Q[h]/(h^{n+1}), deg h^n = 1 (projective bundle formula for Chow groups over a point, SF.5).
c'_j o c_i lies in Corr^{i-j}(Spec(k), Spec(k)), which is zero for i different from j; for i = j it is deg(h^i . h^{n-i}) = 1.
c_i o c'_i is computed on P × Spec(k) × P = P × P as pr_1^*h^{n-i} . pr_2^*h^i; orthogonality and idempotence follow from the previous step.

pi_0 + ... + pi_n = [Delta_P]: this is MC.1/diagonal-of-projective-bundle for X = Spec(k) and E = O^{n+1}, where S^dual has Chern classes c_j(S^dual) = h^j by the Whitney formula for 0 -> S -> O^{n+1} -> O(1) -> 0.

c_i and c'_i restrict to mutually inverse isomorphisms between 1(-i) and (P, pi_i, 0); the decomposition of h(P) follows from the complete family of orthogonal idempotents, since M_k is Karoubian and additive.
acceptance: For n = 1 the projectors are c_0 and c_2 of Example 0FG6, and the decomposition is h(P^1) = 1 + 1(-1).
The sum of the projectors is the diagonal with all coefficients 1: for n = 2, [Delta] = h_1^2 + h_1 h_2 + h_2^2, not the h_1^2 + 2 h_1 h_2 + h_2^2 the printed Lemma 0FGR would give.
The summands are 1(-i) with the twist -i, matching the degree 2i of the cohomology of P^n under any realisation.

sources.excerpt: We immediately conclude c'_j o c_i = 0 for i + r - 1 - j < r - 1, in other words when i < j. On the other hand, [...] Hence for i = j the pushforward above gives the class of the diagonal and hence we see that c'_i o c_i = 1 in Corr^0(X, X)
sources.match: For X = Spec(k) the source's c_i and c'_j are h^i and h^{n-j}; the node specialises that paragraph and Lemma 0FGR (with the correction E9) to projective space.

nodes.title: The diagonal of a projective bundle is the zero scheme of a section
nodes.statement: Let p : P = P(E) -> X be the projective bundle of a locally free module E of rank r on a smooth projective X over k, with p_*O_P(1) = E, let S be the kernel of p^*E -> O_P(1), let q_1, q_2 : P ×_X P -> P be the projections and q = p o q_1. The composite q_1^*S tensor q_2^*O_P(-1) -> q^*E tensor q^*E^dual -> O of the inclusion of S, the dual of the surjection, and the evaluation pairing is a section s of V = q_1^*S^dual tensor q_2^*O_P(1), locally free of rank r - 1; its zero scheme is the diagonal Delta_P, a regular immersion of codimension r - 1, and hence [Delta_P] = c_{r-1}(V) cap [P ×_X P] in CH_*(P ×_X P).
hypotheses: X is smooth projective over k and E is locally free of rank r >= 1.
P ×_X P is smooth over X, so the diagonal, a section of q_1, is a regular immersion.
proofSteps: The statement is local on X; take X = Spec(A) with E free on e_1, ..., e_r, so P ×_X P is P^{r-1}_A ×_A P^{r-1}_A with homogeneous coordinates x and y.

On the chart where x_1 is invertible, S is free on e_j - (x_j/x_1) e_1 for j = 2, ..., r, and the components of s are, up to units, y_j x_1 - x_j y_1 for j = 2, ..., r, whose common zero scheme is the diagonal; the charts cover P ×_X P.
These r - 1 equations form a regular sequence cutting out the diagonal, which has codimension r - 1.

Apply the top Chern class of a section (Stacks 0FA9, imported from SF.5): the zero scheme has the expected dimension and is cut out by a regular sequence at its generic points, so c_{r-1}(V) cap [P ×_X P] = [Delta_P].
acceptance: For r = 1, P = X, V = 0 and the statement is [Delta_X] = [X ×_X X].
For r = 2 and X = Spec(k), P ×_X P = P^1 × P^1 and s is the bihomogeneous form x_2 y_1 - x_1 y_2, up to sign, whose zero scheme is the diagonal.
The section is built from S^dual, not from S: with S in place of S^dual the Chern class has the wrong sign.

sources.excerpt: The source of the composition is a module locally free of rank r - 1 and a local calculation shows that this map vanishes exactly along Delta_P. By Chow Homology, Lemma [top-chern-class] the class [Delta_P] is the top Chern class of the dual q_1^* S dual tensor q_2^* O_P(1)
sources.match: The node is the local calculation the source leaves to the reader, with the hypotheses of Stacks 0FA9 (expected dimension, regular sequence) checked.

nodes.title: Pushforward along a projection integrates over the first factor
nodes.statement: Let H be a classical Weil cohomology theory and X and Y smooth projective varieties, X of dimension d. Then pr_{2,*} : H^*(X × Y) → H^*(Y) sends a ⊗ b = pr_1^*a ∪ pr_2^*b to (∫_X a) b, where ∫_X a is the trace of the component of a in H^{2d}(X), and zero for a of any other degree.
hypotheses: H is a classical Weil cohomology theory; classes on X × Y are written through the Künneth isomorphism.
The trace ∫_X is extended by zero from H^{2d}(X) to all of H^*(X).
proofSteps: By the characterisation in MC.2/weil-pushforward it suffices to show ∫_{X×Y} pr_2^*c ∪ (a ⊗ b) = ∫_Y c ∪ (∫_X a) b for every c in H^*(Y).
pr_2^*c ∪ (a ⊗ b) = (−1)^{|a||c|} a ⊗ (c ∪ b) by graded commutativity; only a of degree 2d contributes to the trace, and then the sign is 1.
Apply MC.2/trace-of-a-product.
acceptance: The source calls this lemma equivalent to the trace formula for a product; given the characterisation of the pushforward each implies the other in one line.
For Y a point it says that the pushforward to a point is the trace.
Classes a of degree other than 2 dim X are sent to zero.

sources.excerpt: Let X and Y be smooth projective varieties. Then pr_{2,*} : H^*(X × Y) → H^*(Y) sends a ⊗ b to (∫_X a) b. Proof. This is equivalent to the result of Lemma 0FGX.
sources.match: The node is Lemma 0FGY, split off from MC.2/trace-of-a-product, with the one-line equivalence written out.

nodes.title: The cycle class of the fundamental class is the unit
nodes.statement: Let H be a classical Weil cohomology theory and X a smooth projective variety. Then H^0(X) is a one-dimensional F-algebra and γ([X]) = 1. Consequently γ(g_*[Z]) = g_*1 for every morphism g : Z → W of smooth projective varieties; in particular γ([Δ]) = Δ_*1 for the diagonal Δ : X → X × X.
hypotheses: H is a classical Weil cohomology theory and X is a smooth projective variety.
g_*[Z] is the proper pushforward of the fundamental cycle, which for a closed immersion is the class of the image.
proofSteps: By (A)(d) and (A)(b), H^0(X) is dual to the one-dimensional H^{2d}(X), so it is a one-dimensional F-algebra, isomorphic to F, with idempotents 0 and 1 only.
[X] · [X] = [X] in CH^*(X) (SF.5), so γ([X]) is idempotent by (C)(c).
For a closed point x, [X] · [x] = [x] and γ([x]) ≠ 0 because its trace is one (MC.2/cycle-class-degree); hence γ([X]) ≠ 0, and γ([X]) = 1.
For g : Z → W, γ(g_*[Z]) = g_*γ([Z]) = g_*1 by (C)(b).
acceptance: The unit of H^*(X) is the class of X itself, not a nonzero multiple of it.
The normalisation (C)(d) enters through the nonvanishing of the class of a point.
For X = Spec k the statement is γ([Spec k]) = 1, which is (C)(d) together with (A)(d).

sources.excerpt: [X] · [X] = [X] hence by axiom (C)(c) the cohomology class γ([X]) is 0 or 1 in the 1-dimensional F-algebra H^0(X); here we have also used axioms (A)(d) and (A)(b). But γ([X]) cannot be zero as [X] · [x] = [x] for a closed point x of X
sources.match: The node is the step of the proof of Lemma 0FGZ showing γ([X]) = 1, made a lemma because Lemmas 0FGZ and 0FH0, the realisation and the round trip all use γ([Δ]) = Δ_*1.

nodes.title: Graded vector spaces with the Koszul sign
nodes.statement: Let F be a field. Integer-graded F-vector spaces form an F-linear symmetric monoidal category with (V ⊗ W)^n = ⊕_{p+q=n} V^p ⊗_F W^q, the usual associativity isomorphisms, unit F placed in degree 0, and commutativity constraint V^p ⊗ W^q → W^q ⊗ V^p, v ⊗ w ↦ (−1)^{pq} w ⊗ v. For an integer n, F[n] denotes F placed in degree −n. An object V has a left dual W exactly when Σ_n dim_F V^n is finite, and then the evaluation gives perfect pairings W^{−n} × V^n → F; the invertible objects are the F[n] up to isomorphism.
hypotheses: The commutativity constraint carries the Koszul sign; the constraint without signs gives a different symmetric monoidal category, which is not the one used here.
F[n] has F in degree −n, so F[2] sits in degree −2.
proofSteps: Build the monoidal structure on integer-graded objects (mathlib:CategoryTheory.GradedObject.monoidalCategory, whose instance hypotheses hold for modules over F).

Twist the degreewise braiding by (−1)^{pq}; naturality, the hexagons and symmetry are the degreewise identities that Tau Ceti proves for the Koszul braiding of cochain complexes (tauceti:TauCeti.koszulSymmetricCategory), restricted to complexes with zero differential, or are checked directly. The source omits this verification.

Left duals: write the coevaluation of 1 as Σ e_{n,i} ⊗ w_{−n,i} in a basis; the zig-zag identities show that W is spanned by the finitely many w_{−n,i}, that V is finite-dimensional and that the w_{−n,i} form the dual basis (Homology Lemma 0FFV).
An invertible object V has a dual W with V ⊗ W ≅ F[0], so its total dimension is one and V ≅ F[n] for some n.
acceptance: The commutativity constraint on F[−1] ⊗ F[−1] is −1.
Graded F-vector spaces of finite total dimension are exactly the dualisable objects.
F[n] ⊗ F[m] ≅ F[n + m].

sources.excerpt: There are two commutativity constraints on C which turn C into a symmetric monoidal category: one involves the intervention of signs and the other does not. We will usually use the one that does. ... V^p ⊗_F W^q → W^q ⊗_F V^p, v ⊗ w ↦ (−1)^{pq} w ⊗ v
sources.match: The node is that example, the convention Lemma 0FH1 uses for graded commutativity; the source omits the verification that it is symmetric monoidal.

sources.excerpt: Let F be a field. Let C be the category of graded F-vector spaces viewed as a monoidal category as in Example 0FFX. If V in C has a left dual W, then Σ_n dim_F V^n < ∞ and the map ε defines nondegenerate pairings W^{−n} × V^n → F.
sources.match: The duality statement of the node.

sources.excerpt: Since 1(1) is invertible in the category of motives we see that G(1(1)) is invertible in the category of graded F-vector spaces. Thus Σ_i dim_F G^i(1(1)) = 1.
sources.match: The description of invertible objects, used there without separate proof.

nodes.title: A classical Weil cohomology theory on smooth projective schemes
nodes.statement: Let H be a classical Weil cohomology theory over an algebraically closed field k. For a smooth projective scheme X over k with connected components X_1, ..., X_n, each a smooth projective variety, set H^*(X) = ∏_i H^*(X_i), with pullback computed componentwise, cycle class map the product of the cycle class maps under CH^*(X) = ⊕_i CH^*(X_i), and, for X equidimensional of dimension d, trace ∫_X = Σ_i ∫_{X_i}. These data satisfy (A)(a), (A)(c) and (B) for all X and Y, (A)(b) for equidimensional X, (C)(a) to (C)(c), and the degree formula of MC.2/cycle-class-degree for equidimensional X; H^0(X) is F^n, so (A)(d) holds exactly when X is connected.
hypotheses: H is a classical Weil cohomology theory over an algebraically closed field k.
X ranges over smooth projective schemes over k, finite disjoint unions of smooth projective varieties, possibly empty and possibly of several dimensions.
The trace is defined only for equidimensional X.
proofSteps: A smooth projective scheme over a field is the disjoint union of its finitely many connected components, each irreducible, hence a smooth projective variety.
A morphism maps each connected component into a connected component, so pullback is defined componentwise and is functorial.

Chow groups of a finite disjoint union are the direct sums of those of the parts, and Gysin pullback, proper pushforward and intersection products are computed componentwise (SF.5); so (C)(a) to (C)(c) and the degree formula reduce to the components.
The components of X × Y are the products X_i × Y_j, so the Künneth maps of the pairs assemble to (B); Poincaré duality for equidimensional X holds componentwise.
acceptance: For X a variety the construction returns H.
H^0(X) has dimension the number of connected components.
The empty scheme has zero cohomology.

sources.excerpt: Since every smooth projective scheme is canonically a disjoint union of smooth projective varieties, it suffices to construct G on the category whose objects are smooth projective varieties and whose morphisms are correspondences of degree 0. (Some details omitted.)
sources.match: The node supplies the omitted details: the extension of a classical theory from varieties to smooth projective schemes (source issue E18).

nodes.title: A Weil cohomology theory for varieties over an arbitrary field
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, k̄ an algebraic closure and H a classical Weil cohomology theory over k̄ with coefficient field A. For a smooth projective scheme X over k set H_k(X) = H^*(X_{k̄}) (MC.2/weil-cohomology-of-schemes), with pullback f^* = (f_{k̄})^*, cycle class map γ_k : CH^r(X) → CH^r(X_{k̄}) → H^{2r}(X_{k̄}) given by flat pullback followed by γ, and trace ∫_{X_{k̄}} for X equidimensional. Then γ_k is compatible with pullback, proper pushforward and intersection products; deg_k(α) = ∫ γ_k(α) for a zero cycle α on an equidimensional X; a correspondence c of degree zero over k acts on H_k by the realisation of c_{k̄}, compatibly with composition; and homological equivalence over k relative to H is the kernel of γ_k on F-linear cycles, for any subfield F of A.
hypotheses: k is any field and H a classical Weil cohomology theory over an algebraic closure of k; Jannsen's example is etale cohomology of X over a separable closure, which gives the same groups.
F is a subfield of A, so that F-linear cycles have cycle classes in A-vector spaces.
Degrees of zero cycles are taken over k.
proofSteps: Base change to k̄ preserves smooth projective schemes and products, and takes morphisms to morphisms.

Flat pullback along X_{k̄} → X commutes with proper pushforward, Gysin pullback and intersection products (Chow Homology Lemmas 0FVJ, 0FVK, 0FVL and 0FVP, from SF.5), so (C)(a) to (C)(c) over k̄ give the compatibilities of γ_k.
The degree of a zero cycle is unchanged by extension of the base field (SF.5), and the degree formula over k̄ holds by MC.2/weil-cohomology-of-schemes.

Base change of correspondences commutes with composition, which is built from the same operations, so c ↦ G(c_{k̄}) is compatible with composition by MC.2/weil-to-monoidal-functor; the universal property MC.1/motives-universal-property then gives a realisation of Chow motives over k.
CH^r(X) ⊗ Q → CH^r(X_{k̄}) ⊗ Q is injective by MC.2/chow-kernel-torsion and MC.2/chow-groups-under-field-extension, so with rational coefficients base change loses no cycles.
acceptance: For k algebraically closed H_k is the theory of MC.2/weil-cohomology-of-schemes.
The cycle class of a closed point of degree n over k has trace n.
Homological equivalence over k refines numerical equivalence over k, because intersection numbers are traces of cup products.

nodes.title: l-adic cohomology is a classical Weil cohomology theory
nodes.statement: Let k be an algebraically closed field and l a prime invertible in k, and choose a generator of Z_l(1) = lim μ_{l^n}(k), which identifies Q_l(r) with Q_l for all r. Then l-adic etale cohomology X ↦ H^*(X, Q_l), with cup product, the l-adic cycle class map and the trace map, is a classical Weil cohomology theory over k with coefficients in Q_l.
hypotheses: k is algebraically closed of any characteristic and l is invertible in k.
The identification Q_l(1) ≅ Q_l is a choice; another generator rescales the cycle class map on CH^r and the trace by powers of a unit of Z_l.
Nothing here constructs etale cohomology or its cycle class map; both are imported.
proofSteps: (D1), (A)(a), (A)(c) and (B): H^*(X, Q_l) is a contravariant functor to graded commutative Q_l-algebras, finite-dimensional, zero outside degrees 0 to 2 dim X, with the Künneth formula for products of smooth projective varieties (SF.2).
(D3), (A)(b) and (A)(d): the trace isomorphism H^{2d}(X, Q_l(d)) → Q_l and Poincaré duality (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.2), transported through the chosen generator.

(D2) and (C): the cycle class map CH^r(X) → H^{2r}(X, Q_l(r)), compatible with Gysin pullback, proper pushforward and intersection products and with trace one on a point (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves:EDC.3).
acceptance: This is the theory that makes Jannsen's theorem unconditional: the proof of c) implies b) needs some Weil cohomology theory over an algebraic closure of every field.
The coefficient field is Q_l with l invertible in k; with l equal to the characteristic one does not get a Weil cohomology theory in this way.
Through MC.2/weil-to-monoidal-functor it gives the l-adic realisation of Chow motives, and through MC.2/weil-cohomology-by-base-change a realisation over any field.

nodes.title: The Lefschetz trace formula for correspondences
nodes.statement: Let H be a classical Weil cohomology theory and X a smooth projective variety of dimension d. For u in H^{2d}(X × X) let φ_u be the endomorphism a ↦ pr_{2,*}(u ∪ pr_1^*a) of H^*(X), which preserves degrees. Then ∫_{X×X} u ∪ γ([Δ]) = Σ_{i=0}^{2d} (−1)^i Tr(φ_u | H^i(X)). In particular, for a correspondence c of degree zero from X to X, deg(c · [Δ]) = Σ_i (−1)^i Tr(G(c) | H^i(X)), with G the realisation of MC.2/weil-to-monoidal-functor.
hypotheses: H is a classical Weil cohomology theory and X is a smooth projective variety of dimension d.
Traces are of F-linear endomorphisms of the finite-dimensional spaces H^i(X).
proofSteps: Take the basis e_{i,j} of H^i(X) and the elements e'_{2d−i,j} of MC.2/class-of-the-diagonal; they form a basis of H^{2d−i}(X), so u = Σ_{i,j,l} u^i_{jl} e'_{2d−i,j} ⊗ e_{i,l}.
By MC.2/pushforward-along-projection and graded commutativity, φ_u(e_{i,m}) = (−1)^i Σ_l u^i_{ml} e_{i,l}, so Tr(φ_u | H^i(X)) = (−1)^i Σ_m u^i_{mm}.
By MC.2/trace-of-a-product and the pairings of MC.2/class-of-the-diagonal, ∫_{X×X} u ∪ γ([Δ]) = Σ_i Σ_m u^i_{mm}; comparing gives the formula.
For a correspondence c, G(c) = φ_{γ(c)} by construction, and deg(c · [Δ]) = ∫ γ(c) ∪ γ([Δ]) by (C)(c) and MC.2/cycle-class-degree.
acceptance: The sign (−1)^i comes from the sign in the Künneth decomposition of the diagonal.
For u = γ([Δ]), φ_u is the identity and the formula is the left-hand equality of MC.2/euler-characteristic-self-intersection.
For a curve C of genus g and c = [Δ], both sides are 2 − 2g.

sources.locator: page 448, Lemma 1, the case g = Δ
sources.excerpt: Then for f, g ∈ B^{dim(X)}(X × X) one has ⟨f · ᵗg⟩ = Σ_{i=0}^{2dim(X)} (−1)^i Tr_i(f ∘ g), where Tr_i(f) is the trace of f acting on H^i(X).

nodes.title: The Künneth components of the diagonal
nodes.statement: Let H be a classical Weil cohomology theory over an algebraic closure of k, extended to k by MC.2/weil-cohomology-by-base-change, and X a smooth projective variety over k of dimension d. The Künneth components of the diagonal are the components π^j of γ_k([Δ]) in H^{2d−j}(X) ⊗ H^j(X), j = 0, ..., 2d, under the Künneth decomposition of H^{2d}(X × X). They sum to γ_k([Δ]); the endomorphism a ↦ pr_{2,*}(π^j ∪ pr_1^*a) is the projection of H^*(X) onto H^j(X); and Tr_i(f ∘ π^j) = δ_{ij} Tr_j(f) for every correspondence f of degree zero. The Künneth components are algebraic if each π^j is γ_k of a Q-linear cycle of dimension d on X × X.
hypotheses: The components depend on H; algebraicity is a property of X relative to H.
Algebraic means in the image of the Q-linear cycles over k, the convention of Kleiman that Jannsen cites; this implies algebraicity with F-linear cycles for any field F of characteristic zero.
proofSteps: Define π^j through the Künneth decomposition of MC.2/weil-cohomology-of-schemes.
By MC.2/pushforward-along-projection the operator of π^j kills H^i for i ≠ j, and on H^j it agrees with the operator of γ_k([Δ]), which is the identity by MC.2/class-of-the-diagonal.
The trace identity follows because f ∘ π^j acts as the action of f composed with the projection onto H^j, and f preserves degrees (MC.2/homological-correspondences-embed).
For products, π^j_{X×Y} = Σ_{r+s=j} π^r_X ⊗ π^s_Y by the Künneth formula, so algebraicity for X and Y gives it for X × Y.
acceptance: The index convention is Jannsen's: π^j lies in H^{2d−j}(X) ⊗ H^j(X) and projects onto H^j(X).
Algebraicity is not automatic; its assertion for all X is Conjecture C (MC.7/kunneth-conjecture-C).
For X a point, π^0 = 1.

sources.locator: page 449, Corollary 1, and page 449 to 450, its proof
sources.excerpt: If, for a variety X, the Künneth components π^j ∈ H^{2dim(X)−j}(X) ⊗ H^j(X) of the diagonal are algebraic (cf. [K1] Sect. 2), then ... Now, by definition of the π^j we have Tr_i(f ∘ π^j) = δ_{ij} Tr_j(f) for every f ∈ B
sources.match: The definition and the defining trace identity; placed in MC.2 so that MC.3 does not depend on MC.7, which states the conjecture that they are algebraic.

sources.excerpt: Moreover, if the assumption holds for X and Y, it also holds for X × Y, since π^j_{X×Y} = Σ_{r+s=j} π^r_X ⊗ π^s_Y by the Künneth formula.

nodes.title: Realisation of correspondences is faithful modulo homological equivalence
nodes.statement: Let H be a classical Weil cohomology theory over an algebraic closure of k with coefficient field A, extended to k by MC.2/weil-cohomology-by-base-change, F ⊆ A a subfield, and X and Y smooth projective varieties over k with X of dimension d. The action c ↦ (a ↦ pr_{2,*}(γ_k(c) ∪ pr_1^*a)) of F-linear correspondences of degree r from X to Y on cohomology vanishes exactly on the homologically trivial ones, maps H^i(X) to H^{i+2r}(Y), and is compatible with composition. Hence it induces an injective map A_hom^{d+r}(X × Y, F) → ⊕_i Hom_A(H^i(X), H^{i+2r}(Y)), which for X = Y and r = 0 is an injective homomorphism of F-algebras from B = A_hom^{d}(X × X, F) to ⊕_i End_A(H^i(X)).
hypotheses: F is a subfield of the coefficient field A of H.
Homological equivalence is relative to H, through γ_k.
Composition of correspondences is Jannsen's, g ∘ f = p_{13,*}(p_{12}^*f · p_{23}^*g), and goes to composition of maps.
proofSteps: By Künneth and Poincaré duality (MC.2/weil-cohomology-of-schemes), u ↦ (a ↦ pr_{2,*}(u ∪ pr_1^*a)) is an isomorphism from H^{2d+2r}(X × Y) onto ⊕_i Hom_A(H^i(X), H^{i+2r}(Y)); the degree shift is read off from MC.2/pushforward-along-projection.
So the action of c is zero exactly when γ_k(c) = 0, that is, when c is homologically trivial (MC.2/homological-equivalence).
Compatibility with composition is the functoriality of MC.2/weil-to-monoidal-functor, transported to k by MC.2/weil-cohomology-by-base-change.
acceptance: A realisation factors through homological equivalence for the theory used and is faithful there; this is the precise quotient relation the stage asks a realisation to factor through.
It does not factor through numerical equivalence unless numerically trivial cycles are homologically trivial, which is Conjecture D (MC.7/conjecture-D); nothing here assumes it.
For X = Y and c the diagonal, the image is the identity of each H^i(X).

sources.excerpt: By definition, the cycle map B ↪ H^{2dim(X)}(X × X) = ⊕_{i≥0} End H^i(X) is an injective ring homomorphism, so that f is nilpotent in B.
sources.match: The node is the statement Jannsen uses as a definition, with the identification of H^{2d}(X × X) with the endomorphisms of cohomology made explicit and extended to correspondences between two varieties.

nodes.title: The two constructions of Proposition 0FH3 are mutually inverse
nodes.statement: Let k be algebraically closed and F of characteristic zero. (a) If H is a classical Weil cohomology theory, G_H its realisation (MC.2/weil-to-monoidal-functor) and F[2] → G_H(1(1)) the normalisation given by ∫_{P^1}, then the data that MC.2/weil-from-monoidal-functor recovers from this pair are those of H: G_H(h(f)) = f^* for every morphism f, and the recovered cup product, cycle class maps and trace maps are those of H. (b) If G is a Q-linear symmetric monoidal functor with an isomorphism F[2] → G(1(1)) satisfying the two conditions of MC.2/realization-equivalence, and H is the classical theory it determines, then G_H is isomorphic to G as a symmetric monoidal functor, compatibly with the normalisations.
hypotheses: k is algebraically closed and F has characteristic zero.
The normalisations are part of the data on both sides.
proofSteps: (a), pullback: for f : Y → X, γ([Γ_f]) = (f, id)_*1 by MC.2/cycle-class-of-fundamental-class, and the projection formula of MC.2/weil-pushforward gives pr_{Y,*}((f, id)_*1 ∪ pr_X^*a) = f^*a.
(a), cup product: the recovered product is pullback along the diagonal composed with the Künneth map, which is the cup product (Remark 0FGU).

(a), cycle classes and traces: a cycle α in CH^r(X), viewed as a correspondence from Spec k to X, acts by 1 ↦ γ(α), because the projection Spec k × X → X is an isomorphism; the identification F[−2r] → G_H(1(−r)) is the r-th power of the one given by ∫_{P^1}, which matches it with γ. The trace is G_H of [X] : h(X)(d) → 1, which is the pushforward to a point, that is ∫_X, by MC.2/pushforward-along-projection.

(b): a correspondence c of degree zero from X to Y corresponds under the duality of MC.1/motive-dual to a morphism 1 → h(X)(d) ⊗ h(Y); monoidality of G and the zig-zag identities express G(c) as a ↦ pr_{2,*}(γ(c) ∪ pr_1^*a), which is G_H(c). The identifications are natural and monoidal, and they match the normalisations because both are fixed on (P^1, c_2, 0) (MC.1/lefschetz-motive).
acceptance: Both round trips are checked, not only the two constructions; without them Proposition 0FH3 gives two maps between the two classes and no bijection.
The normalisation is what makes cycle classes and traces come back exactly and not up to scalars.
For G coming from H the recovered theory has the Betti numbers of H.

sources.excerpt: A classical Weil cohomology theory is the same thing as a Q-linear functor G : M_k → graded F-vector spaces of symmetric monoidal categories together with an isomorphism F[2] → G(1(1)) ... Conversely, given H^* we get a functor G by the construction of Lemma 0FH2.
sources.match: The proposition asserts a bijection; its proof builds the two constructions and checks the extra conditions but does not compose them (source issue E13). The node supplies the verification.

nodes.title: Graphs and the duality pairings
nodes.statement: Let f : Y → X be a morphism of smooth projective schemes over k, with X and Y equidimensional of dimensions d and e. Write a = [Γ_f] in Corr^0(X, Y), a^t = [Γ_f^t] in Corr^{d−e}(Y, X), η_X and η_Y for the classes of the graphs of the diagonal morphisms in Corr^0(X × X, X) and Corr^0(Y × Y, Y), and [X] in Corr^{−d}(X, Spec k), [Y] in Corr^{−e}(Y, Spec k). Then [Y] ∘ η_Y ∘ (a ⊗ id) = [X] ∘ η_X ∘ (id ⊗ a^t) as correspondences from X ⊗ Y to Spec k.
hypotheses: X and Y are equidimensional smooth projective schemes over k and f : Y → X is a morphism.
Composition and tensor product are those of MC.0/correspondence-composition and MC.0/tensor-of-correspondences.
proofSteps: Correspondences to Spec k are cycles, Corr^r(W, Spec k) = CH_{−r}(W), and composing with a correspondence is pulling back by it (MC.0/composition-associative).
Along the top: (a ⊗ id)^*η_Y^*[Y] = (a ⊗ id)^*[Δ_Y] = (f × id)_*[Δ_Y] = [Γ_f], by MC.0/graph-acts-as-gysin-and-pushforward.
Along the bottom: (id ⊗ a^t)^*η_X^*[X] = (id ⊗ a^t)^*[Δ_X] = (id × f)^![Δ_X] = [Γ_f], by Chow Homology Lemma 0FF7 (from SF.5).
Both are the class of Γ_f in Corr^d(X × Y, Spec k).
acceptance: Both composites are the class of the graph of f, viewed as a cycle on X × Y.
This is what turns axiom (C)(b) into an identity of morphisms of motives in Lemma 0FH1.
For f the identity both composites are the class of the diagonal.

nodes.title: The kernel of base change on Chow groups is torsion
nodes.statement: Let K over k be an algebraic field extension and X a scheme of finite type over k. The kernel of flat pullback CH_i(X) → CH_i(X_K) is torsion. In particular CH_i(X) ⊗ Q → CH_i(X_K) ⊗ Q is injective.
hypotheses: K over k is algebraic and X is of finite type over k.
Chow groups are integral; the torsion statement is about them.
proofSteps: By MC.2/chow-groups-under-field-extension a class that dies in CH_i(X_K) already dies over a finite subextension k'.
For π : X_{k'} → X, finite flat of degree [k' : k], π_*π^*α = [k' : k] α (Chow Homology Lemma 02RH, from SF.5), so a class killed by π^* is killed by [k' : k].
acceptance: The kernel is torsion, not zero: integral Chow groups need not inject under base change.
With rational coefficients the map is injective, which is what a realisation over a non-closed field needs.
For K = k the kernel is zero.

nodes.title: Zero cycles are generated by separable points
nodes.statement: Let k be a field and X a smooth projective scheme over k. Then CH_0(X) is generated by the classes of closed points whose residue fields are separable over k.
hypotheses: k is any field; the content is for imperfect k.
X is smooth and projective over k.
proofSteps: If k is perfect every finite extension is separable; so assume k is an infinite field of characteristic p > 0.

Reduce to X irreducible of dimension d; k' = Γ(X, O_X) is a finite separable extension over which X is geometrically integral (Stacks Varieties Lemmas 056T, 0BUG and 0FD1), and replacing k by k' is harmless.

For a closed point x choose an ample invertible sheaf L, replaced by a power so that sections vanishing at x generate L away from x, give an immersion of X minus x, and surject onto m_x L_x / m_x^2 L_x (Varieties Lemma 0FD5, Properties Proposition 01Q3, Morphisms Lemma 01VU).
For general sections s_1, ..., s_d vanishing at x and generating m_x L_x / m_x^2 L_x, Bertini's theorem (Varieties Lemma 0FD6) makes H_1 ∩ ... ∩ H_d = x ⊔ Z with Z etale over k.

By the proper intersection formula (Chow Homology Lemma 0FFD, from SF.5), [H_1] ⋯ [H_d] = [x] + [Z]; comparing with a general complete intersection Z' etale over k gives [x] = [Z'] − [Z] in CH_0(X). The source leaves the repeated use of the proper intersection formula with details omitted.
acceptance: Over a perfect field the statement is empty; its content is for imperfect fields.
The class of a point is a difference of classes of etale zero cycles, not in general a positive combination.
The proof uses projectivity through an ample invertible sheaf.

nodes.title: Semisimple abelian categories
nodes.statement: An abelian category C is semisimple if every object of C is a finite direct sum of simple objects. Equivalently, every object has finite length and every short exact sequence in C splits. When C is F-linear with finite-dimensional Hom spaces, the endomorphism ring of a simple object is a division algebra over F, and C is equivalent to a direct sum, indexed by the isomorphism classes of simple objects, of categories of finite-dimensional vector spaces over these division algebras.
hypotheses: C is abelian; simple objects are those of mathlib:CategoryTheory.Simple.
Finite direct sums are biproducts; the empty sum is the zero object.
The block decomposition is stated for F-linear C with finite-dimensional Hom spaces, the setting of Jannsen's Lemma 2.
proofSteps: Define the predicate on an abelian category.

Prove the splitting characterisation: a finite sum of simples has finite length and every subobject is a summand, and conversely a finite composition series of an object all of whose short exact sequences split exhibits it as a sum of simples.
Prove Schur's lemma for simple objects (the endomorphism ring is a division ring) and group the simple summands by isomorphism class to get the block decomposition.
acceptance: A semisimple abelian category is abelian by hypothesis; the predicate adds the decomposition.
In a semisimple abelian category every monomorphism and every epimorphism splits.
Invariance under equivalence of categories.

sources.excerpt: Indeed, then C is equivalent to a sum, indexed by the isomorphism classes of indecomposables (= irreducibles), of categories which are equivalent to categories of vector spaces over skewfields.

nodes.title: Trace and rank in a rigid symmetric monoidal category
nodes.statement: Let T be an F-linear symmetric monoidal category with End(1) = F, and M an object with a dual M^∨, coevaluation η : 1 → M ⊗ M^∨ and evaluation ε : M^∨ ⊗ M → 1. The trace of an endomorphism u of M is Tr(u) = ε ∘ β_{M, M^∨} ∘ (u ⊗ id) ∘ η in End(1) = F, where β is the commutativity constraint, and the rank of M is rk(M) = Tr(id_M). The trace does not depend on the choice of dual, is symmetric, Tr(u ∘ v) = Tr(v ∘ u), and is preserved by F-linear symmetric monoidal functors; so if a symmetric monoidal functor to vector spaces over an extension F' of F exists, rk(M) is the dimension of the image of M.
hypotheses: T is F-linear and symmetric monoidal with End(1) = F.
The trace depends on the commutativity constraint: changing the constraint changes ranks.
proofSteps: Define the trace by the displayed composite, with Mathlib's exact pairings for the duality data.
Independence of the dual: two duals are related by a unique isomorphism compatible with the pairings.
Symmetry and multiplicativity: the usual string-diagram identities in a symmetric monoidal category.
Preservation by symmetric monoidal functors: such a functor takes duality data to duality data and the constraint to the constraint.
acceptance: In finite-dimensional vector spaces the trace is the usual trace.
rk(1) = 1 and rk(M ⊗ N) = rk(M) rk(N).
The trace depends on the constraint, which is the point of Jannsen's sign change.

sources.excerpt: In an abelian category T with tensor products and duals it possible to deﬁne the trace of an endomorphism of an object. This is preserved by every exact faithful tensor functor ω: T → Vec_Q, and so, for the identity map u of an object M, Tr(u|M) = Tr(ω(u)|ω(M)) = dim_Q ω(M)

nodes.title: Tannakian categories
nodes.statement: Let F be a field of characteristic zero. A Tannakian category over F is an F-linear abelian rigid symmetric monoidal category T with End(1) = F for which there exist an extension field F' of F and a fibre functor with values in F', that is, an exact, faithful, F-linear symmetric monoidal functor from T to finite-dimensional F'-vector spaces. It is neutral if there is a fibre functor with values in F itself.
hypotheses: The fibre functor is required only over some extension field of F; neutrality is a separate condition.
The symmetric monoidal structure, including the commutativity constraint, is part of the data: one abelian tensor category can be Tannakian for one constraint and not for another.
proofSteps: Define the predicate from the data of a fibre functor.
Record that every object then has rank a nonnegative integer (MC.3/categorical-rank), the dimension of its image under a fibre functor.
Define neutrality as the existence of a fibre functor over F.
acceptance: Tannakian categories have nonnegative integer ranks.
Neutral Tannakian categories are Tannakian.
The predicate is invariant under symmetric monoidal equivalence.

nodes.title: Numerical cycle groups are finite-dimensional
nodes.statement: Let k be a field and suppose a classical Weil cohomology theory over an algebraic closure of k is given. For every smooth projective variety X over k and every j, the Q-vector space A^j_num(X, Q) of Q-linear cycles of codimension j modulo numerical equivalence is finite-dimensional, and for every field F of characteristic zero the natural map A^j_num(X, Q) ⊗_Q F → A^j_num(X, F) is an isomorphism. In particular the numerical correspondence spaces A^{dim X + r}_num(X × Y, F) are finite-dimensional.
hypotheses: k is any field; some classical Weil cohomology theory over an algebraic closure of k is given, for instance l-adic cohomology (MC.2/etale-cohomology-is-weil).
X is smooth projective over k; the result does not depend on the theory used.
proofSteps: Homologically trivial cycles are numerically trivial, and intersection numbers are traces of cup products of cycle classes (MC.2/homological-equivalence, MC.2/weil-cohomology-by-base-change).
The cycle classes of the Q-cycles of codimension dim X − j span a finite-dimensional subspace of H^{2 dim X − 2j}(X); choose cycles z_1, ..., z_s whose classes span it.

The map A^j_num(X, Q) → Q^s, x ↦ (⟨x · z_1⟩, ..., ⟨x · z_s⟩), is injective: if all ⟨x · z_i⟩ vanish, then for any cycle z write γ(z) = Σ λ_i γ(z_i), and ⟨x · z⟩ = ∫ γ(x) ∪ γ(z) = Σ λ_i ⟨x · z_i⟩ = 0. Hence dim A^j_num(X, Q) ≤ s.

The pairing A^j_num(X, Q) × A^{dim X − j}_num(X, Q) → Q is nondegenerate by definition; with dual bases, an F-linear combination of Q-cycles is numerically trivial exactly when its coefficients in the basis vanish, which gives the isomorphism with F coefficients.
acceptance: The dimension is bounded by a Betti number: dim A^j_num(X, Q) ≤ dim H^{2 dim X − 2j}(X), which equals dim H^{2j}(X) by Poincaré duality.
Rational equivalence gives no such finiteness: for an elliptic curve E over the complex numbers, CH^1(E) ⊗ Q is infinite-dimensional.
The statement is unconditional, but it uses the existence of a Weil cohomology theory.

nodes.title: The radical of a finite-dimensional algebra commutes with field extension
nodes.statement: Let A be a finite-dimensional algebra over a field E of characteristic zero and K an extension field of E. Then the Jacobson radical of K ⊗_E A is K ⊗_E J(A). In particular K ⊗_E A is semisimple if and only if A is.
hypotheses: E has characteristic zero, so every finite extension of E is separable.
A is finite-dimensional over E; K is any extension field.
proofSteps: K ⊗_E J(A) is a nilpotent two-sided ideal of K ⊗_E A, since J(A) is nilpotent (A is Artinian, mathlib:IsSemiprimaryRing), so it lies in the radical.
The quotient by it is K ⊗_E (A/J(A)), and A/J(A) is a finite product of simple algebras by Artin–Wedderburn; so it suffices that K ⊗_E S is semisimple for a finite-dimensional simple E-algebra S.
S is central simple over its centre L, a finite, hence separable, extension of E, and K ⊗_E S = (K ⊗_E L) ⊗_L S with K ⊗_E L a finite product of fields K_i.

Each K_i ⊗_L S is simple (tauceti:TauCeti.IsSimpleRing.tensorProduct, with centrality from tauceti:TauCeti.Algebra.IsCentral.baseChange) and finite-dimensional over K_i, hence semisimple; so the quotient is semisimple and the radical lies in K ⊗_E J(A).
acceptance: Characteristic zero is used: over an imperfect field the radical can grow under inseparable extension.
For A semisimple the statement is that K ⊗_E A is semisimple.
For K = E it is trivial.

sources.excerpt: In particular, the Jacobson radical J of A^{dim(X)}(X × X, F) is obtained from the one of A^{dim(X)}(X × X, Q) by base extension to F, and it suffices to show J = 0 over any field F.

nodes.title: An endomorphism with vanishing power traces is nilpotent
nodes.statement: Let V be a finite-dimensional vector space over a field A of characteristic zero and φ an endomorphism of V with Tr(φ^n) = 0 for every n ≥ 1. Then φ is nilpotent.
hypotheses: A has characteristic zero.
V is finite-dimensional.
proofSteps: Over an algebraic closure of A the characteristic polynomial splits with roots λ_1, ..., λ_m, m = dim V, and Tr(φ^n) = Σ λ_i^n (mathlib:Matrix.trace_eq_sum_roots_charpoly applied to φ^n, whose characteristic roots are the λ_i^n).

Newton's identities (mathlib:MvPolynomial.psum_eq_mul_esymm_sub_sum) express n e_n through the power sums p_1, ..., p_n; the power sums vanish and n is invertible, so every elementary symmetric function e_n with n ≥ 1 vanishes.
Hence the characteristic polynomial is X^m and φ is nilpotent (mathlib:LinearMap.isNilpotent_iff_charpoly).
acceptance: Characteristic zero is needed: in characteristic p the identity of a p-dimensional space has all power traces zero and is not nilpotent.
Only traces of powers of φ are used.
For φ = 0 the statement is trivial.

sources.excerpt: The same is true for all powers of f, which implies that for all i ≥ 0 the endomorphism f_i of H^i(X) induced by f has zero eigenvalues, thus is nilpotent.

nodes.title: A semisimple category of motives forces numerical equivalence
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, F of characteristic zero and ∼ an adequate relation on F-linear cycles. If the category M_k of motives modulo ∼ is a semisimple abelian category, then ∼ is numerical equivalence.
hypotheses: k is any field, F has characteristic zero and ∼ is adequate.
Only the unit object and the objects (X, id, j) are used.
proofSteps: End(1) = A^0(Spec k) = F is a field, so the unit 1 = (Spec k, id, 0) is a simple object.

For an irreducible variety X and a nonzero f in A^j(X) = Hom(1, (X, id, j)) (MC.0/composition-associative), f is a monomorphism, its kernel being a proper subobject of the simple object 1; by semisimplicity it splits, giving g : (X, id, j) → 1 with g ∘ f = id.
In terms of cycles, g lies in A^{dim X − j}(X) and g ∘ f = p_*(f · g) = ⟨f · g⟩ = 1 in F = A^0(Spec k), p the structure morphism; so no nonzero class of A^j(X) is numerically trivial.

Hence every numerically trivial cycle is ∼-trivial, that is, ∼ is at least as coarse as numerical equivalence; since numerical equivalence is the coarsest adequate relation (MC.0/adequate-equivalence-relation), ∼ is numerical equivalence.
acceptance: With rational equivalence the category is not semisimple as soon as some numerically trivial cycle is not rationally trivial.
The argument shows that ∼ is at least as coarse as numerical equivalence, not finer.
For X = Spec k it is the statement A^0(Spec k) = F.

nodes.title: Numerical correspondences form semisimple algebras
nodes.statement: Let k be a field and F a field of characteristic zero, and suppose a classical Weil cohomology theory over an algebraic closure of k is given. Then for numerical equivalence, A^{dim X}(X × X, F) is a finite-dimensional semisimple F-algebra for every variety X over k.
hypotheses: k is any field and F has characteristic zero.
Some classical Weil cohomology theory over an algebraic closure of k is given; the conclusion does not depend on it.
proofSteps: By MC.3/numerical-cycles-finite-dimensional, A^{dim X}(X × X, F) is finite-dimensional and is A^{dim X}(X × X, Q) ⊗ F; by MC.3/radical-base-change its radical is the base change of the radical over Q, so it suffices to show that the radical vanishes for one coefficient field of characteristic zero, which we take to be the coefficient field A of the theory.

With F = A, let B be the A-linear correspondences of degree zero on X modulo homological equivalence; B embeds in ⊕_i End_A(H^i(X)) (MC.2/homological-correspondences-embed), so it is finite-dimensional, and S : B → A^{dim X}(X × X) is a surjection of finite-dimensional A-algebras.
Let J' be the radical of B. B/J' is semisimple (mathlib:IsSemiprimaryRing), hence so is its quotient by S(J'), and S(J') is nilpotent; so S(J') is the radical J of A^{dim X}(X × X).

For f in J choose f' in J' with S(f') = f. For every g in B, f' ∘ g lies in J' and is nilpotent, so its action on each H^i(X) is nilpotent and has trace zero (mathlib:LinearMap.isNilpotent_trace_of_isNilpotent).
By MC.3/trace-formula-for-correspondences, ⟨f' · ᵗg⟩ = Σ (−1)^i Tr_i(f' ∘ g) = 0 for all g; as ᵗg runs through B, f' is numerically trivial, so f = S(f') = 0.
acceptance: The Weil cohomology theory enters only through the finite dimensionality of B and the trace formula; the conclusion is about numerical equivalence alone.
The argument does not use that homological and numerical equivalence agree.
For X = Spec k the algebra is F.

sources.excerpt: Now consider the surjection of finite-dimensional Q_l-algebras S : B = B^{dim(X)}(X × X) → A^{dim(X)}(X × X) = A and let J' be the Jacobson radical of B. Since B/J' is semi-simple and this carries over to quotients, and since S(J') is a nilpotent two-sided ideal in A, we must have S(J') = J.

nodes.title: Semisimple correspondence algebras give a semisimple category
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, F of characteristic zero and ∼ adequate. If A^{dim X}(X × X) is a finite-dimensional semisimple F-algebra for every variety X, then the category M_k of motives modulo ∼ is a semisimple abelian category.
hypotheses: k is any field, F has characteristic zero and ∼ is adequate.
The hypothesis is on varieties; the argument transfers it to all objects.
proofSteps: For an object (X, p, m), End((X, p, m)) = p A^{dim X}(X × X) p, which does not depend on m; so it suffices to treat direct factors M of h(X) = (X, id, 0).

Write h(X) = M ⊕ N. A nilpotent two-sided ideal J of End(M) generates the ideal of End(h(X)) with corners J, J ∘ Hom(N, M), Hom(M, N) ∘ J and Hom(M, N) ∘ J ∘ Hom(N, M); a product of n of its elements has entries in the corners built from J^{n−1}, so the ideal is nilpotent, hence zero, and J = 0.
A finite-dimensional algebra without nonzero nilpotent two-sided ideals is semisimple (mathlib:IsSemiprimaryRing), so End(M) is finite-dimensional semisimple for every object M.
M_k is F-linear and pseudo-abelian (MC.1/motives-mod-adequate-relation); apply MC.3/pseudo-abelian-semisimplicity.

Jannsen notes that this implication is well known and includes it for convenience.

nodes.title: Cohomology of a numerical motive
nodes.statement: Let k be a field, H a classical Weil cohomology theory over an algebraic closure of k with coefficient field A ⊇ F, and X a smooth projective variety over k whose Künneth components are algebraic. For a numerical motive M = (X, p, m), p lifts to an idempotent p' of A_hom^{dim X}(X × X, F); any two idempotent lifts are conjugate by a unit; and H^i(M) = p' H^{i+2m}(X) is well defined up to non-canonical isomorphism. Moreover Tr_i descends to numerical classes, and Tr_{i+2m}(p) = dim_A H^i(M).
hypotheses: The Künneth components of X are algebraic, so that MC.3/radical-of-homological-correspondences applies.
H^i(M) is defined up to non-canonical isomorphism only; this is not a functor on numerical motives.
proofSteps: By MC.3/radical-of-homological-correspondences the kernel of A_hom^{dim X}(X × X, F) → A_num^{dim X}(X × X, F) is a nilpotent ideal, and idempotents lift along a surjection with nil kernel (mathlib:exists_isIdempotentElem_eq_of_ker_isNilpotent).

Two idempotent lifts p' and p'' are conjugate: u = p''p' + (1 − p'')(1 − p') is congruent to 1 modulo the nilpotent kernel, hence a unit, and u p' = p'' u; so p''H^j(X) = u(p'H^j(X)). Jannsen cites Murre for this lemma, which was not obtained; this is the standard argument.
By MC.3/radical-of-homological-correspondences numerically trivial classes have vanishing traces, so Tr_i descends to A_num, and for an idempotent lift Tr_i(p) = Tr_i(p') = dim_A p'H^i(X).
acceptance: A faithful realisation of numerical motives would need Conjecture D; this lemma only gives cohomology up to isomorphism.
The hypothesis is algebraicity of the Künneth components for X only.
For M = h(X), H^i(M) = H^i(X).

sources.excerpt: Under the assumption of Corollary 1, one can associate cohomology groups H(M) to every motive M = (X, p, m) w.r.t. numerical equivalence, such that H(M) is well-defined up to non-canonical isomorphism. In fact, one can lift p to an idempotent p' in A_hom^{dim X}(X × X)

nodes.title: The quotient from Chow motives to numerical motives
nodes.statement: Let k be a field and F a field of characteristic zero. There is an F-linear symmetric monoidal functor from the motives for rational equivalence with F-linear cycles to the motives for numerical equivalence with F-linear cycles (both instances of MC.1/motives-mod-adequate-relation), sending (X, p, m) to (X, p̄, m), where p̄ is the numerical class of p, and a morphism to its numerical class. It is full, its kernel on each Hom space consists of the numerically trivial morphisms, and every numerical motive is a direct summand of the image of a Chow motive.
hypotheses: F has characteristic zero; with F = Q the source is the category of Chow motives of MC.1, and in general its extension of scalars.
Both categories carry the commutativity constraint induced by the switch of factors.
proofSteps: Rational equivalence is finer than numerical equivalence (MC.0/adequate-equivalence-relation), so reduction of cycles gives surjective F-linear maps A_rat^{dim X − m + n}(X × Y) → A_num^{dim X − m + n}(X × Y) compatible with composition, both composition laws being induced by the same operations on cycles.
Idempotents map to idempotents; define the functor on objects and on morphisms by reduction.
It is full because the maps on correspondences are surjective, and symmetric monoidal because both tensor structures come from products of cycles and the switch of factors.
A numerical motive (X, e, m) is a direct summand of (X, id, m), the image of h(X)(m).
acceptance: The functor is the identity on underlying schemes and twists.
It is not faithful in general.
Every realisation of numerical motives would factor a realisation of Chow motives through it, which for a Weil cohomology theory is Conjecture D.

nodes.title: Inverting an object of a symmetric monoidal category
nodes.statement: Let (C, tensor, 1) be a symmetric monoidal category and T an object. The category C[T^{-1}] has objects the pairs (X, m) with X in C and m an integer, and Hom((X, m), (Y, n)) is the colimit over i (with m + i and n + i nonnegative) of Hom(X tensor T^{tensor(m+i)}, Y tensor T^{tensor(n+i)}), the transition maps being given by tensoring with T; composition is induced from C. The functor C -> C[T^{-1}], X -> (X, 0), satisfies (X, m) = X tensor T^{tensor m} for m >= 0, and (X, m) tensor (T, 0) is isomorphic to (X, m + 1). If C is additive, respectively tensor triangulated, so is C[T^{-1}] and the functor is additive, respectively triangulated. If the cyclic permutation of T^{tensor 3} is the identity in C[T^{-1}], then (X, m) tensor (Y, n) = (X tensor Y, m + n) makes C[T^{-1}] symmetric monoidal, and tensor triangulated when C is. If tensoring with T is fully faithful on C, the functor C -> C[T^{-1}] is fully faithful.
hypotheses: C is symmetric monoidal; for the triangulated statements C is tensor triangulated in the sense of MVW Definition 8A.1.
The symmetric monoidal structure needs the cyclic permutation hypothesis; without it C[T^{-1}] need not be symmetric monoidal (MVW Exercise 8A.9).
proofSteps: Define objects and Hom groups as filtered colimits along tensoring with T; compose by representing two morphisms at a common level; check associativity and identities.

Triangulated structure (MVW Exercise 8A.8, stated as an exercise): shift (X, m)[1] = (X[1], m); call a triangle distinguished when it is isomorphic to the image of a distinguished triangle of C twisted by some (-, m); verify the axioms at a finite level of the colimit.

Symmetric monoidal structure (MVW Proposition 8A.10): define f tensor g on representatives; the choices, indexed by shuffles, differ by permutations of powers of T, which commute with each other when the cyclic permutation of T^{tensor 3} is the identity; the hexagon axiom follows from the same hypothesis.
Compatibility of the two structures (MVW Corollary 8A.11).
Full faithfulness when tensoring with T is fully faithful: every transition map is then bijective (compare MVW Exercise 8A.12).
acceptance: For T the unit the functor C -> C[T^{-1}] is an equivalence.
(T, 0) is invertible, with inverse (1, -1).
Every object is isomorphic to (X, -n) for some n >= 0 and X in C.

sources.excerpt: Let C[T^-1] denote the category whose objects are pairs (X,m) with X in C and m in Z; morphisms (X,m) -> (Y,n) in C[T^-1] are just elements of the direct limit lim_{i->infinity} Hom(X tensor T^{tensor m+i}, Y tensor T^{tensor n+i}), where the bonding maps are given by the functor tensor T : C -> C.
sources.match: The construction, literally.

sources.excerpt: Let T be an object in a symmetric monoidal category (C,tensor,1) such that the cyclic permutation on T^{tensor 3} is the identity in C[T^-1]. Then (C[T^-1],tensor,1) is also a symmetric monoidal category.
sources.match: The symmetric monoidal structure and its hypothesis; 8A.11 adds the triangulated structure under the same hypothesis.

sources.excerpt: Let T be an object in a tensor triangulated category C. Show that C[T^-1] is a triangulated category, and that C -> C[T^-1] is triangulated.
sources.match: The triangulated structure, left as an exercise in the source and planned here.
