nodes.title: Finite subdiagrams give the motivic Galois group as a pro-algebraic group
nodes.statement: Let C(T) be a rigid diagram category over a field k as in MC.6/tensor-automorphism-group. For a finite subdiagram F let X_F be the direct sum of the objects attached to the vertices of F and C_F the full subcategory of C(T) whose objects are the subquotients of objects P(X_F, X_F^∨), P a polynomial with natural number coefficients. Then C_F is a neutral Tannakian category with algebraic Tannaka group G_F, a closed subgroup of GL(f_T(X_F ⊕ X_F^∨)); for F ⊂ F′ the restriction G_{F′} → G_F is faithfully flat; and G(T) is the projective limit of the G_F, that is, A(T) is the directed union of the finitely generated Hopf subalgebras A_F = O(G_F).
hypotheses: C(T) is rigid over a field k, as in MC.6/tensor-automorphism-group.
F runs through the finite subdiagrams of the diagram, ordered by inclusion.
proofSteps: C_F is a rigid abelian tensor subcategory with tensor generator X_F ⊕ X_F^∨, so its Tannaka group is algebraic (Deligne and Milne, Proposition 2.20(b)) and embeds in GL of the fibre of the generator.
For F ⊂ F′ the inclusion C_F → C_{F′} is fully faithful and closed under subquotients, so G_{F′} → G_F is faithfully flat (Proposition 2.21(a)).

Every object of C(T) is a subquotient of a finite sum of objects attached to vertices (Proposition B.9), hence lies in some C_F; by Deligne and Milne's Proposition 2.14 the coordinate ring is the colimit of the coordinate rings of the C_F, so A(T) is the directed union of the A_F.
Conclude that G(T) is the projective limit of the algebraic groups G_F.
acceptance: For a finite diagram the group G(T) = G_D is algebraic.
Each G_F is a closed subgroup of a general linear group, through the representation on f_T(X_F ⊕ X_F^∨).
The finite pieces A(F, T) of Nori's colimit are coalgebras, not Hopf algebras; the Hopf subalgebras are the A_F of the tensor subcategories they generate.

sources.locator: Propositions 2.14, 2.20 and 2.21 (pages 22 to 25), in the corrected version of 2012
sources.excerpt: PROPOSITION 2.20. Let G be an afﬁne group scheme over k. (a) G is ﬁnite if and only if there exists an object X of Repk(G) such that every object of Repk(G) is isomorphic to a subquotient of Xn for some n ≥ 0. (b) G is algebraic if and only if Repk(G) has a tensor generator X.
sources.match: The algebraicity of the groups of the subcategories generated by finite subdiagrams, with Propositions 2.14 and 2.21 for the colimit and the transition maps.

sources.locator: Proposition B.7 and Proposition B.9 (pages 17 to 18), arXiv:1105.0865v5
sources.excerpt: Let A(F, T ) := HomR(End(T |F ), R). We set A(T ) := colimF A(F, T ). Then C(T ) is the category of ﬁnitely generated R-modules with an R-linear A(T )-comodule structure.
sources.match: Nori's colimit over finite subdiagrams, and the generation of C(T) by the objects attached to vertices.

nodes.title: The comparison isomorphism as a complex point of the period torsor
nodes.statement: Let φ : H*_dR ⊗ C → H* ⊗ C be the comparison isomorphism between algebraic de Rham and singular cohomology of pairs of varieties over Q, natural in morphisms of pairs, compatible with connecting maps and with products (request SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.6). Then φ defines a complex point of X_{1,2} = Iso⊗(H*_dR, H*), that is, a Q-algebra homomorphism per : A_{1,2} → C sending the class of (p, ω, γ) to γ(φ_p(ω)). Composed with P = A_{1,2} (MC.6/formal-periods-equal-comparison-algebra) it is a ring homomorphism P → C. This is the coefficient embedding of the period torsor that the layer exports to PeriodsAndSpecialValues.
hypotheses: The comparison isomorphism is an isomorphism of graded multiplicative representations of the diagram of pairs after extension of scalars to C (request SF.6).
No rational point of X_{1,2} is asserted.
proofSteps: Read φ as a compatible family of complex linear maps T_1(p) ⊗ C → T_2(p) ⊗ C commuting with the edges and respecting products, that is, a tensor isomorphism T_1 ⊗ C → T_2 ⊗ C.
By MC.6/tensor-iso-scheme this is a complex point of X_{1,2}, a Q-algebra map A_{1,2} → C, and its value on the class of (p, ω, γ) is γ(φ_p(ω)).
Compose with P = A_{1,2} to obtain a ring homomorphism P → C.
acceptance: When the comparison is the integration pairing, the value on the class of (G_m, {1}, dX/X, S^1) is 2πi, as the source records; the identification with integration is proved in PeriodsAndSpecialValues:PS.2.
The point is a point of the torsor: under the heap map it satisfies φ φ⁻¹ φ = φ.
The injectivity of the resulting map P → C is the period conjecture and is not claimed.

sources.locator: Introduction, the paragraph after Theorem 0.2 (page 2), arXiv:1105.0865v5
sources.excerpt: ... singular cohomology and algebraic de Rham cohomology are both ﬁber functors on the same Tannaka category of motives. By general Tannaka formalism, there is a pro-algebraic torsor of isomorphisms between them. The period pairing is nothing but a complex point of this torsor.
sources.match: The node makes that sentence a construction.

sources.excerpt: All formal eﬀective periods (X, D, ω, γ) can be evaluated by ”integrating” ω along γ. More precisely, there is a natural pairing Hd dR(X, D) × Hd(X(C), D(C)) → C This induces a ring homomorphism ev : P → C which maps (Gm, {1}, dX/X, S1) to 2πi.
sources.match: The evaluation, which PeriodsAndSpecialValues:PS.2 constructs by integration and identifies with this point.

nodes.title: Hodge classes
nodes.statement: Let X be a projective non-singular algebraic variety over C and n ≥ 0. The complex cohomology H^n(X, C) = H^n(X, Q) ⊗ C carries the Hodge filtration F^p, which this packet takes to be the image of the hypercohomology of the truncated algebraic de Rham complex Ω^{≥p} under the comparison of algebraic de Rham and singular cohomology (ComplexComparisonPartII:C5); by the Hodge decomposition, which no layer of the atlas plans (gap), F^p = ⊕_{a ≥ p} H^{a, n−a}. A Hodge class of degree 2p is an element of H^{2p}(X, Q) whose image in H^{2p}(X, C) lies in F^p. The Hodge classes form the Q-subspace H^{2p}(X, Q) ∩ F^p, which equals H^{2p}(X, Q) ∩ H^{p,p}.
hypotheses: X is projective and non-singular over C.

F^p is the image of the hypercohomology of Ω^{≥p}; its identification with ⊕_{a ≥ p} H^{a, n−a}, and the equality H^{2p}(X, Q) ∩ F^p = H^{2p}(X, Q) ∩ H^{p,p}, use the Hodge decomposition and its symmetry (gap).
Integral classes are Hodge classes when their rational images are.
proofSteps: Define the Hodge filtration on algebraic de Rham cohomology through the truncations Ω^{≥p}, and transport it to H^n(X, C) by the comparison isomorphism of ComplexComparisonPartII:C5.
Define the Hodge classes of degree 2p as the preimage of F^p under H^{2p}(X, Q) → H^{2p}(X, C), a Q-subspace.
Record Deligne's equality with H^{2p}(X, Q) ∩ H^{p,p}, which needs the Hodge decomposition and Hodge symmetry (gap).

Record functoriality: pullback along a morphism of smooth projective complex varieties preserves the filtration, hence Hodge classes, and cup product sends Hodge classes of degrees 2p and 2q to a Hodge class of degree 2(p + q).
acceptance: The Hodge classes are a Q-subspace of rational cohomology; the complex subspace F^p is not the definition.
Every class of H^0(X, Q) is a Hodge class, and so is every class of H^{2N}(X, Q) for X of dimension N (the latter through the Hodge decomposition).
The class of an algebraic cycle of codimension p is a Hodge class (MC.7/cycle-classes-are-hodge), but in general not in F^{p+1}.

sources.locator: Section 1, the paragraph on the Hodge filtration and the paragraph before the statement (page 1 to 2)
sources.excerpt: When X moves in a holomorphic family, the Hodge ﬁltration F p := ⊕a≥p Ha,n−a of Hn(X, C) is better behaved than the Hodge decomposition. ... Rational (p, p)-classes are called Hodge classes. They form the group H2p(X, Q) ∩ Hp,p(X) = H2p(X, Q) ∩ F p ⊂ H2p(X, C).
sources.match: The definition of the Hodge filtration and of Hodge classes, verbatim; the packet's algebraic description of F^p is the one the de Rham comparison supplies.

nodes.title: The class of an algebraic cycle is a Hodge class
nodes.statement: Let X be a projective non-singular variety over C and Z a closed analytic subspace of complex codimension p, by Chow's theorem the same as an algebraic cycle. The class cl(Z) in H^{2p}(X, Z), defined by Poincaré duality, is of type (p, p): its image in H^{2p}(X, C) lies in F^p, so its rational image is a Hodge class. Hence every rational linear combination of cycle classes is a Hodge class.
hypotheses: X is projective and non-singular over C; Z is a closed analytic, equivalently algebraic, subspace of codimension p.
The argument computes cohomology with currents; that currents compute the same groups as smooth forms, and the Hodge decomposition, are recorded as a gap.
proofSteps: Use Chow's theorem to identify closed analytic subspaces of X with algebraic cycles (ComplexComparisonPartII:C4).
Compute H^n(X, C) and the H^{p,q} with currents instead of smooth forms, which gives the same groups.
Represent the image of cl(Z) in H^{2p}(X, C) by the integration current on Z, a closed (p, p)-form with generalised function coefficients.
Conclude that the image of cl(Z) is of type (p, p), hence lies in F^p, and pass to rational combinations.
acceptance: The lemma makes the Hodge conjecture a surjectivity statement.
The class of a hyperplane section is a Hodge class of degree 2 not lying in F^2.
The lemma holds integrally: the integral class cl(Z) is of type (p, p).

sources.locator: Section 1, the last paragraph of page 1 and the first sentence of page 2, and remark (i) of Section 2
sources.excerpt: If Z is a closed analytic subspace of X, of complex codimension p, Z is an integral cycle and, by Poincaré duality, deﬁnes a class cl(Z) in H2p(X, Z). The integration current on Z is a closed (p, p)-form with generalized function coeﬃcients, representing the image of cl(Z) in H2p(X, C).
sources.match: The node is that argument; remark (i) supplies Chow's theorem.

nodes.title: The strong Tate conjecture
nodes.statement: Let k be finitely generated over its prime field, X smooth projective over k and l invertible in k. The strong Tate conjecture for (X, a) is the conjunction of the Tate conjecture for (X, a) with the assertion that the Galois-invariant subspace of H^{2a}(X_{k_s}, Q_l(a)) is a direct summand as a Galois representation. The source records that several proofs of cases of the Tate conjecture, such as divisors on abelian varieties, give the strong form, that the strong form would imply most of Grothendieck's standard conjectures except the Hodge standard conjecture in positive characteristic, in particular that numerical and homological equivalence coincide, and that over a finite field it would describe the category of Grothendieck motives: every motive would be a Tate twist of a summand of the motive of an abelian variety tensored with an Artin motive.
hypotheses: k finitely generated over its prime field, X smooth projective, l invertible in k, coefficients Q_l.

The implications to the standard conjectures and to the description of motives over finite fields are recorded from the source; their proofs (André's book, Milne's motives over finite fields) were not obtained and they are not planned.
proofSteps: Take the Tate predicate of MC.7/tate-conjecture.
Define the summand condition: there is a Galois-stable complement to the Galois-invariant subspace.
Define the strong predicate as the conjunction.
Record the source's statements about its consequences, without proofs.
acceptance: Over a finite field the summand condition says that the Frobenius acts semisimply on its generalised eigenspace for the eigenvalue one.
The strong predicate implies the Tate predicate by projection.
No node uses the recorded consequences as theorems.

sources.locator: Section 2, the paragraphs on the strong Tate conjecture and on motives over finite fields (pages 6 to 7)
sources.excerpt: The strong Tate conjecture is the combination of the Tate conjecture with the conjecture that, for a smooth projective variety over a ﬁnitely generated ﬁeld k, the Galois-invariant subspace of H2a(X, Ql(a)) is a summand, as a Galois representation.
sources.match: The definition, verbatim; the consequences are recorded from the two paragraphs that follow.

nodes.title: The Tate-Beilinson conjecture
nodes.statement: Let X be a smooth projective variety over a finite field k and l invertible in k. Beilinson's injectivity for (X, a) asserts that the cycle map CH^a(X) ⊗ Q → H^{2a}(X_{k_s}, Q_l(a)) is injective. The Tate-Beilinson conjecture for (X, a), the strengthening of the Tate conjecture in Totaro's account, is the conjunction of the Tate conjecture with Beilinson's injectivity. The source records that injectivity holds for a = 1, because the group of rational points of an abelian variety over a finite field is finite, that beyond this case evidence is limited, with cases due to Soulé and Kahn, and that the analogue is false over other fields: for an elliptic curve X, CH^1(X) is Z ⊕ X(k) and X(k) maps to zero in H^2.
hypotheses: k is a finite field; X is smooth projective over k; l is invertible in k; coefficients Q_l.
The codimension-one case is recorded from the source; its proof uses the Picard variety and is not planned here.
proofSteps: Take the cycle map to geometric l-adic cohomology (request SF.2) and the rational Chow groups (request SF.5).
Define Beilinson's injectivity as the injectivity of the cycle map tensored with Q.
Define the Tate-Beilinson predicate as its conjunction with the Tate predicate.
Record the codimension-one case and the failure over other fields as the source states them.
acceptance: The Tate-Beilinson predicate implies the Tate predicate, as in the source's diagram.
Over C the analogous injectivity fails already for divisors on an elliptic curve, whose degree-zero part is uncountable and maps to zero.
No node uses the predicate as a hypothesis without naming it.

sources.locator: Section 2, the paragraphs on the Tate-Beilinson conjecture (page 7)
sources.excerpt: ... there is an important strengthening of the Tate conjecture, the Tate-Beilinson conjecture. Namely, let X be a smooth projective variety over a ﬁnite ﬁeld k. ... Beilinson conjectured in the mid-1980s that the cycle map to l-adic cohomology, CHa(X) ⊗ Q → H2a(X, Ql(a)), is injective

gaps.title: The conditions in Murre's conjecture and in the Bloch-Beilinson filtration are in no source read here
gaps.detail: Milne's notes say that Murre conjectured a decomposition of the diagonal modulo rational equivalence with certain properties, and that his conjecture is equivalent to the existence of a filtration on the Chow groups conjectured by Beilinson and Bloch. The properties and the filtration axioms are what give both statements their content, and neither is stated in any source read for this packet. The node states the part that is precise, the existence of a Chow-level orthogonal idempotent decomposition, and records the rest as missing. NEXT SOURCE ACTION: obtain Murre's two 1993 papers in Indagationes Mathematicae, or Jannsen's article on motivic sheaves and filtrations on Chow groups in the 1991 motives proceedings, and add the conditions verbatim before anything is built on them.

gaps.title: The proofs behind the K3 entries of the register were not read
gaps.detail: Totaro's survey attributes the Tate conjecture for K3 surfaces over finite fields to a series of papers by Charles, Kim, Madapusi Pera and Maulik, with the elliptic case due to Artin and Swinnerton-Dyer and the non-supersingular case to Nygaard and Ogus. The survey's sketch of the elliptic case was read; the technical sections on the other two were not, and the original papers were not obtained. The register records each entry with its attribution and its hypotheses as the survey states them, and claims nothing beyond that. NEXT SOURCE ACTION: obtain Madapusi Pera's and Kim-Madapusi Pera's papers for the supersingular case, and Nygaard-Ogus for the non-supersingular case, before any of these entries is used as an input to another statement.

gaps.title: Algebraic equivalence and its implications are not planned
gaps.detail: The MC.0 brief asks for rational, algebraic, homological and numerical equivalence with the proved implications. Algebraic equivalence is not defined in any source this packet read (the Stacks chapters Weil Cohomology Theories and Chow Homology do not define it; checked by searching both LaTeX sources at the pinned commit; Jannsen and Milne mention it only by name). Missing: the definition (a class is algebraically trivial when it is a difference of two fibres of a cycle on X × T over two rational points of a smooth connected curve T, up to finite extensions of the base field), the proof that it is adequate in the sense of MC.0/adequate-equivalence-relation, and the implications rational => algebraic => homological (for a classical Weil cohomology theory) and algebraic => numerical. NEXT SOURCE ACTION: obtain a public source with the definition and the adequacy proof (for example Fulton, Intersection Theory, Section 10.3, through a library copy) and add three nodes to MC.0.

gaps.title: Kleiman's 1968 survey, which Jannsen cites for the trace formula, finite dimensionality and Künneth components, was not obtained
gaps.detail: Jannsen cites Kleiman's 'Algebraic cycles and the Weil conjectures' for three inputs: the trace formula (1.3.6), the finite dimensionality of numerical cycle groups with the isomorphism A^j(X, Q) ⊗ F → A^j(X, F) (Theorem 3.5), and the notion of algebraic Künneth components (Section 2). The survey was not obtained. The nodes do not rest on it: MC.2/lefschetz-trace-formula is derived from Lemmas 0FGZ and 0FH0 of the Stacks chapter, MC.3/trace-formula-for-correspondences from that formula and an identity of correspondences, MC.3/numerical-cycles-finite-dimensional by the standard argument through a Weil cohomology theory, and MC.2/kunneth-components follows Jannsen's own description. A continuation job should obtain the survey and compare each statement with its source.

gaps.title: Deligne's Tannakian criterion, and the definitions of rank and of a Tannakian category in the works Jannsen cites, were not obtained
gaps.detail: The last step of Corollary 2 applies Deligne's theorem 7.1 of 'Catégories tannakiennes' (a rigid abelian tensor category over a field of characteristic zero with End(1) equal to the field, all of whose objects have nonnegative integer rank, is Tannakian). Jannsen also takes the rank from Deligne and Milne, 'Tannakian categories', p. 113, and the notion of Tannakian category from Saavedra Rivano and Deligne. None of these was obtained. MC.3/categorical-rank and MC.3/tannakian-category use the standard definitions, with Milne's expository description as source; everything in Corollary 2 up to the nonnegativity of the modified ranks is decomposed from Jannsen's text, and the final implication rests on the cited criterion.

gaps.title: Murre's lifting lemma, cited for Remark 4, was not obtained
gaps.detail: Jannsen's Remark 4 cites 'the lemma in [M] 7.3 bis' of Murre's 1990 paper for lifting a numerical idempotent to a homological one and for the conjugacy of two lifts. The paper was not obtained. The node proves both by the standard ring-theoretic argument (lifting along a surjection with nilpotent kernel, which Mathlib provides, and conjugation by u = p''p' + (1 − p'')(1 − p')), so it does not rest on the citation; a continuation job should compare.

gaps.title: Friedlander-Voevodsky's shifting and duality theorems are cited without proof in the source read
gaps.detail: MVW cite Theorem 16.22 (the shifting theorem for bivariant cycle cohomology) from [BivCy, 8.3] and Theorem 16.24 (duality) from [BivCy, 8.2], and say of the latter 'We also cite it without proof'. The Kuenneth map for motives with compact support that Corollary 16.16 uses belongs to the same theory. Every statement of MC.4 about duals, rigidity and the embedding of Chow motives rests on 16.24. NEXT SOURCE ACTION: obtain Friedlander and Voevodsky, 'Bivariant cycle cohomology', in Cycles, transfers and motivic homology theories (Annals of Math. Studies 143), and decompose Theorems 8.2 and 8.3.

gaps.title: The Gysin triangle and the smooth blow-up formula over a perfect field without resolution of singularities
gaps.detail: MVW state Corollary 15.13 with no hypothesis and Theorem 15.15 over a perfect field, but the proof of 15.13 uses Theorem 13.26, which assumes resolution of singularities (and, through 13.25, a perfect field); 15.15 is proved from 15.13 (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles/E21). The nodes carry the hypothesis the proof uses, so the Gysin triangle and the layer's boundary-map acceptance test are planned only over perfect fields with resolution, in particular in characteristic zero. NEXT SOURCE ACTION: obtain Voevodsky, 'Triangulated categories of motives over a field' (the same Annals volume), whose blow-up and Gysin statements are proved over any perfect field, and replace the dependency on 13.26.

gaps.title: The functor from Chow motives to geometric motives is asserted, not constructed, in the source read
gaps.detail: MVW Proposition 20.1 proves an isomorphism Hom_Chow(Y, X) = Hom(M(X), M(Y)) for each pair of smooth projective schemes; Remark 20.2 then speaks of a diagram of fully faithful tensor functors, but compatibility of these isomorphisms with composition and with the tensor product is not shown (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles/E24). The node records the bijections and does not build on a functor. NEXT SOURCE ACTION: Voevodsky's 'Triangulated categories of motives over a field' constructs the functor; obtain it.

gaps.title: Transfers and flat and proper functoriality of the sheaves of equidimensional cycles are not proved in the source read
gaps.detail: MVW leave the transfer structure on z_equi(T, r) as Exercise 16.3 (with the hint to use Fulton's identity 2.2(4)) and cite the flat and proper functoriality from Suslin-Voevodsky, 'Relative cycles and Chow sheaves' 3.6.2 and 3.6.4. NEXT SOURCE ACTION: obtain 'Relative cycles and Chow sheaves' (same Annals volume) or plan the exercise from the hint; the theory of relative cycles is also what MotivicEtaleKTheory:M.5a needs for finite correspondences, so the supplier should be asked first.

gaps.title: Nori's Basic Lemma is stated without proof in the source read
gaps.detail: HMS Lemma D.2 is stated with attributions to Nori, Beilinson ([B, Lemma 3.3]) and Vilonen and no proof. It is the geometric input of the very good filtrations (Corollaries D.11 and D.12) and hence of the realisation functor of Proposition D.3. NEXT SOURCE ACTION: obtain Beilinson, 'On the derived category of perverse sheaves' (LNM 1289), Lemma 3.3, or Nori's 'Constructible sheaves'.

gaps.title: The realisation functor on complexes of varieties is only sketched in the source read
gaps.detail: The proof of HMS Proposition D.3 constructs R on objects and morphisms and asserts that other choices give isomorphic complexes, but does not verify that R is triangulated or that H^j(R(Cone(Y -> X))) is concentrated in degree i with the stated value (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles/E31). The node lists the missing verifications. NEXT SOURCE ACTION: obtain the authors' book 'Periods and Nori motives' (2017), which reworks the yoga of good pairs, and decompose its proof.

gaps.title: The product of a coboundary edge with a pair is not defined in the source read
gaps.detail: The proof of HMS Theorem 1.6 gives the product structure on the diagram of good pairs on vertices only. For a coboundary edge (Y, Z, i) -> (X, Y, i + 1) and a vertex (X', Y', j), a product edge or path from (Y x X', Y x Y' union Z x X', i + j) to (X x X', X x Y' union Y x X', i + j + 1) is needed; the only coboundary edges into the target start at pairs (X x Y' union Y x X', V), and a path of functoriality edges to one of them would need a map X x Y' union Y x X' -> Y x X' restricting to the identity, which does not exist when Y is not a retract of X (for example Y two points of X = A^1) (MotivesAndAlgebraicCycles/E30). A repair: enlarge the diagram by excision edges, which singular cohomology sends to isomorphisms, so that the diagram category is unchanged by Proposition B.9(3) and the universal property. NEXT SOURCE ACTION: compare with the authors' 2017 book.

gaps.title: The primary sources for the known cases of Conjecture C were not obtained
gaps.detail: The register of known cases of the algebraicity of the Kuenneth projectors records four cases: dimension at most two, abelian varieties, base fields inside the algebraic closure of a finite field, and products. Only the product case is proved in a source read for this packet. The other three are attributed by Jannsen to Murre's 1990 paper on the motive of an algebraic surface, to Lieberman as reported in Kleiman's 1968 survey, and to Katz and Messing's 1974 paper, none of which was obtained. The node stands on Jannsen's report of them and says so. Katz and Messing argue through the Riemann hypothesis for varieties over finite fields; the continuation must check which Weil cohomology theories their result covers before the case is used for an arbitrary theory in the sense of MC.2. Milne's notes state the abelian-variety case only in characteristic zero. A continuation job should obtain the three papers and either confirm each case or restate it with the hypotheses of its own source.

gaps.title: The universal property of Nori's diagram category is not proved in the source read
gaps.detail: The diagram category is used in MC.5 and MC.6 through its universal property (Proposition B.8), which is what lets a representation into an abelian category with a faithful exact functor to vector spaces factor through it; the extension of the second fibre functor in MC.6 and the comparison of the diagrams of pairs, good pairs and very good pairs are exactly such factorisations. The source states the universal property and says in its introduction that the proof is not included in its account and is supplied by von Wangenheim's work, which was not obtained. The nodes that use it name it in their statements, and no node of this packet asserts a proof of it. For the tensor version used by MC.6/fibre-functor-extension the multiplicative form of the universal property (Proposition B.16) is needed as well.

gaps.title: The Artin and Tate subcategories of Nori motives are computed in no source read
gaps.detail: The acceptance of MC.6 asks to calculate the Artin and Tate subcategories and their tensor automorphism groups. Huber and Mueller-Stach's paper does not compute them, and no node of this packet does. The Tate subcategory is the rigid abelian tensor subcategory of Nori motives generated by 1(−1); the Artin subcategory is generated by the motives H^0 of zero-dimensional varieties over Q. Computing their Tannaka groups needs, for the first, that the objects 1(−n) are pairwise non-isomorphic and that the subcategory has no nontrivial extensions, and for the second a description of H^0 of finite étale Q-schemes as Galois sets. NEXT SOURCE ACTION: obtain a source that computes them, for example Huber and Mueller-Stach's book Periods and Nori Motives, and add the two computations as nodes of MC.6.

gaps.title: The quotient theorem of SGA 3 used for Proposition A.6 was not obtained
gaps.detail: Proposition A.6 of Huber and Mueller-Stach forms the left and right groups of an affine heap as affine quotients of X × X, citing Theorem 1.4 of SGA 3, Exposé VII, for the existence of affine quotients by flat equivalence relations. That text was not obtained, so the step is recorded, not decomposed. The proposition is not on the path to the period torsor, where the acting groups are the tensor automorphism groups and no quotient is formed.

gaps.title: The Hodge decomposition of a smooth projective complex variety is planned by no layer
gaps.detail: Deligne's statement of the Hodge conjecture uses the Hodge decomposition H^n(X, C) = ⊕ H^{p,q} of a compact Kähler manifold, the Hodge filtration F^p = ⊕_{a≥p} H^{a,n−a}, Hodge symmetry, the computation of cohomology with currents and the identification of H^{0,2} with H^2(X, O) used by the degree-two case. The Tau Ceti roadmap HodgeStructures builds abstract Hodge structures (its layer L0), not the Hodge theorem for varieties, and ComplexComparisonPartII:C5 builds the algebraic de Rham comparison without the degeneration of the Hodge-to-de Rham spectral sequence. MC.7/hodge-class therefore defines F^p algebraically, through the truncated de Rham complex and C5's comparison, and records its identification with the analytic filtration, the (p, p) description of Hodge classes, the lemma MC.7/cycle-classes-are-hodge (through currents) and the degree-two register entry as depending on this gap. NEXT ACTION: the maintainer chooses an owner for the Hodge theorem for smooth projective complex varieties, for example a Part II of HodgeStructures or of ComplexComparison.

gaps.title: The precise Hodge standard conjecture, and the Lefschetz standard conjecture for an arbitrary Weil cohomology theory, are in no source read
gaps.detail: Milne's notes name the Lefschetz and Hodge standard conjectures and describe the second as a positivity statement, without stating either. Deligne's problem description gives, over C, the class z_p inverting hard Lefschetz (Section 4, Example 2), which this packet uses to type a Lefschetz predicate for l-adic and Betti cohomology, with hard Lefschetz from DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.9. The identification of that predicate with Grothendieck's Lefschetz standard conjecture for an arbitrary Weil cohomology theory, the positivity form of the Hodge standard conjecture with its sign and primitive decomposition, and the implication from the Lefschetz standard conjecture to Conjecture C are in no source read, so the Hodge standard conjecture is not typed. NEXT SOURCE ACTION: Milne, Polarizations and Grothendieck's standard conjectures (arXiv:math/0103175), or Kleiman's article The standard conjectures in the 1991 Motives proceedings.

gaps.title: The primary proofs of the Hodge and Tate register entries were not obtained
gaps.detail: Every entry of the register except the K3 entries (a separate gap) stands on a survey: the degree-two Hodge entry on Deligne's sketch of Kodaira and Spencer's proof; Tate's theorem on Totaro's sketch with Zarhin's trick; Faltings's theorem on its owner FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems:R28.4 (requested); Zarhin's extension, the h^{2,0} = 0 case, Tankeev's, André's and Moonen's theorems, and Beilinson's injectivity in codimension one on Totaro's report. The stage allows proving a case only after its primary proof is acquired, so the register records these entries and proves none. NEXT SOURCE ACTION: obtain Tate (1966), Zarhin, Tankeev, André (1996) and Moonen (2017) for the entries a downstream layer needs first.

gaps.title: Two steps of the Stacks Project's proof of smash nilpotence are omitted in the source
gaps.detail: The proof of Lemma 0FH9 asserts, with details omitted, that the norm along π : X^n → S^n(X) satisfies π^*Norm_π(L_1) = (L_1 ⊗ ... ⊗ L_n)^{⊗(n−1)!} (findings E46) and that S^n(X) → Pic^n_{X/k} is a projective space bundle for n ≥ 2g − 1 (finding E47). Both are standard, and the second is close to Picard Schemes of Curves, Lemma 44.6.7, which the proof points to; they must be proved, or supplied by SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.3 (request extended), before the node is built.

requests.need: The comparison isomorphisms between the realisations: Betti against de Rham over an embedding into the complex numbers, and etale against Betti with finite and l-adic coefficients. For MC.6: for every pair (X, Y) of varieties over Q with Y closed in X, the comparison isomorphism between relative algebraic de Rham cohomology H^i_dR(X, Y) ⊗ C and relative singular cohomology H^i(X(C), Y(C), Q) ⊗ C, natural for morphisms of pairs, compatible with the connecting maps of triples and with products (Künneth and cup product), so that it is an isomorphism of graded multiplicative representations of the diagram of pairs after extension of scalars; Huber and Mueller-Stach cite Huber's Mixed realizations, sections 7 and 8, for it. ComplexComparisonPartII:C5 owns the case of smooth and of proper smooth varieties; the extension to pairs of arbitrary varieties must be supplied here or requested from C5. For MC.7: the compatibility of the Betti and de Rham cycle classes under the comparison (MC.7/cycle-classes-are-hodge), and the comparison of l-adic and Betti cohomology over C used to transport hard Lefschetz. This packet takes these as given from the owner of the comparison theorems.

Bloch's higher Chow groups CH^i(X, m) defined by the simplicial cycle complexes z^i(X, *) (MVW 17.1), with homotopy invariance and Bloch's localisation theorem (MVW 17.4), the structure of presheaves with transfers on their homology (MVW 17.21), Suslin's comparison of higher Chow groups with equidimensional cycles over affine schemes (MVW 18.3), Zariski descent for the cycle complexes (MVW 19.12, from the localisation theorem and the Brown-Gersten theorem 19.11), the Bloch-Levine pullbacks with their agreement with pullback by graphs (MVW 19.13-19.16), the vanishing CH^i(X, m) = 0 for m < 0, and the weight-one identification Pic(X) = H^{2,1}(X, Z) (MVW 4.2). The comparison in MC.4 identifying motivic cohomology with higher Chow groups is one half of an isomorphism between an object this packet imports from M.5a and an object M.4 owns; RS-08 assigns the cycle complexes to M.4 and the comparison to this roadmap.

Finite correspondences between smooth schemes and their composition, presheaves and Nisnevich sheaves with transfers (MVW Lectures 1, 2, 6, 13) with the exactness of the Cech complex of a Zariski cover as Nisnevich sheaves with transfers (MVW 6.12, 6.14); the A^1-localisation DM^eff,-_Nis(k,R) with the motive M(X) of a smooth scheme and its tensor triangulated structure with M(X) tensor M(Y) = M(X x Y) (MVW 14.1, 14.2, 8.10); the motivic complexes R(q) = C_*R_tr(G_m^{wedge q})[-q] with R(1)^{tensor q} = R(q) and their multiplication maps (MVW 3.1, 2.13, 10.4); representability H^{n,i}(X, R) = Hom(M(X), R(i)[n]) and the internal Hom RHom(M(X), -) of MVW 14.12 and 14.16; Theorem 13.8, Corollary 13.14 and Proposition 11.2 on homotopy invariant presheaves with transfers over a perfect field; Nisnevich excision (MVW 12.20); the cdh topology with Lemma 12.30 and Theorem 13.25 (over a perfect field with resolution, C_*(F) is acyclic when F_cdh = 0); pullback of relative cycles and pushforward along finite maps (MVW Appendix 1A); and Voevodsky's cancellation theorem over a perfect field: for K, L in DM^eff,-_Nis(k), Hom(K, L) -> Hom(K(1), L(1)) is bijective (arXiv:math/0202012, Corollary 4.10), with R-coefficients. MC.4 builds the geometric subcategory, the Tate stabilisation, the Gysin and blow-up triangles and the comparison with higher Chow groups on these and plans none of them; RS-08 assigns them to M.5a.

Chow groups CH_*(X) and CH^*(X) with rational equivalence for schemes of finite type over a field, with the following, each named by its Stacks tag in the chapter Chow Homology and Chern Classes: proper pushforward and its functoriality (02R5); flat pullback, its functoriality, and flat pullback against proper pushforward in a fibre square (02RG); lci Gysin maps, with the Gysin map of a flat morphism equal to flat pullback (0FF4), composition of Gysin maps (0FF5), the easy case of the Gysin map of a transversal fibre square (0FF7) and compatibility of Gysin maps with the intersection product (0FFB); the intersection product on smooth schemes with its associativity (0FC1), commutativity and the projection formula (0FFC); the proper intersection formula (0FFD) and the formula for intersecting with a regularly embedded closed subscheme (0FFE); the degree of a zero cycle on a proper scheme and its compatibility with proper pushforward; exterior products and their compatibility with flat pullback, proper pushforward and intersection products; the Chow groups of a disjoint union as a direct sum; Chern classes of locally free modules with capping commuting with proper pushforward (02U9), the Chern classes of a twist by an invertible module (02UD) and the Whitney formula; the top Chern class of a section with zero scheme of the expected codimension (0FA9); and the projective bundle formula for Chow groups (02TX). Every one of these is cited by name in the construction of correspondences, of Chow motives and of the projective bundle formula for motives, and none is planned in this packet; the reviewed audit of SF.5 records all of them as absent from both pinned libraries, and RS-18 and RS-25 name SF.5 as their owner. In addition, for MC.2 and MC.3: the exterior product with α × β = pr₁*α · pr₂*β (stated without proof in Stacks Remark 0FGU); the self-intersection formula for a regular immersion (0FFE, 0FBM) with the conormal sheaf of the diagonal equal to Ω_{X/k} (Morphisms 08S2); the fundamental class as unit of the intersection ring; c₁(O_C(D)) ∩ [C] = [D] for a divisor on a curve; for change of base field, flat pullback along X_K → X compatible with proper pushforward, Gysin maps and intersection products (0FVJ, 0FVK, 0FVL, 0FVP), invariance of the degree of a zero cycle, Chow groups of a limit (0FVQ) and π_*π^* = deg for finite flat π (02RH). For MC.7: the first Chern class operations on Chow groups with c_1(L)^m ∩ α = 0 when L is pulled back from a scheme of dimension less than m (Chow Homology, Lemma 42.34.6), the description of invertible modules on a projective space bundle trivial on the fibres as pullbacks (Lemma 42.36.2), exterior products of cycles, the rational Chow groups CH^a(X) ⊗ Q of a smooth projective variety over a finite field, and π_*π^* = [k′ : k] for a finite extension (Lemma 42.15.2).

For every algebraically closed field k and every prime l invertible in k: l-adic etale cohomology H^i(X, Q_l) of smooth projective varieties over k as a contravariant functor to graded commutative Q_l-algebras under cup product, finite-dimensional, zero outside degrees 0 to 2 dim X, with the Künneth isomorphism for products X × Y. The trace, Poincaré duality and cycle class map are requested from EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.2 and EDC.3, and MC.2/etale-cohomology-is-weil assembles them into a classical Weil cohomology theory. Algebraic de Rham and Betti cohomology are used only through the comparison requested from SF.6 for MC.6. In addition, for MC.5, MC.6 and MC.7: relative singular cohomology and homology of pairs (X(C), Y(C)) with rational coefficients and relative algebraic de Rham cohomology of pairs of arbitrary (possibly singular) varieties over Q, functorial for morphisms of pairs, with the connecting maps of triples and with products (MC.5 and MC.6/formal-periods); geometric l-adic cohomology H^i(X_{k_s}, Q_l(a)) of a variety over an arbitrary field k with its continuous Galois action and Tate twists, the Galois-equivariant cycle class map from cycles on X, its compatibility with proper pushforward along finite morphisms, and l-adic Borel-Moore homology of arbitrary varieties (the Tate nodes of MC.7); Betti cohomology of X(C) with integral and rational coefficients and its cycle class map (the Hodge nodes of MC.7).

For varieties over Q: the space X(C) of complex points with the analytic topology, functorial in X, as a topological space in Mathlib's TopCat; finite-dimensionality of the relative singular cohomology H^*(X(C), Y(C); Q) for a closed subvariety Y; the relative Kuenneth isomorphism and the compatibility of the cross product with the coboundaries of triples; excision for proper maps that are isomorphisms outside a closed subset (proper base change as used in HMS Corollary 1.8); the Thom isomorphism H^0(Z) -> H^{2n}_Z(X) for a smooth closed subvariety of pure codimension n of a smooth variety, with the Kuenneth formula with supports; and Poincare-Lefschetz duality between the pairs (W - W_inf, W_0 - W_0 intersect W_inf) and (W - W_0, W_inf - W_0 intersect W_inf) for W smooth projective with a normal crossings divisor W_0 union W_inf. Relative singular homology with the long exact sequence of a triple is already in the pinned Tau Ceti library; MC.5 plans cohomology as its dual and plans none of the above.

Smooth projective curves with their divisors and the degree map, and normal crossings divisors on a smooth projective variety (the generators of Nori motives in MC.5); the degree 2g − 2 of the canonical divisor of a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus g; for every field k a smooth projective geometrically connected curve of genus 2 over k; and, for hyperplane sections, Bertini's theorem over an infinite field in the form of Stacks Varieties Lemma 0FD6, with the ample-sheaf lemmas used with it (Varieties 0FD5, Properties 01Q3, Morphisms 01VU) and the facts that Γ(X, O_X) of a smooth proper irreducible X is a finite separable extension over which X is geometrically integral (Varieties 056T, 0BUG, 0FD1). For MC.7/smash-nilpotence also: the Picard schemes Pic^n of a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve over an algebraically closed field, the symmetric powers S^n(X) = Hilb^n_{X/k} with the finite flat morphism X^n → S^n(X) of degree n!, norms of invertible modules along finite locally free morphisms, the morphism S^n(X) → Pic^n being a projective space bundle for n ≥ 2g − 1, and Bertini's theorem giving a smooth curve through two given points of a smooth projective variety of dimension at least two over an algebraically closed field (Stacks, Picard Schemes of Curves, Sections 44.2, 44.3 and Lemma 44.6.7; Divisors, Section 31.18; Varieties, Lemmas 33.47.1, 33.47.3 and 33.48.3).

For k algebraically closed, l invertible in k and X smooth projective of pure dimension d over k: the trace map H^{2d}(X, Q_l(d)) → Q_l, an isomorphism for X connected, and perfectness of the cup product pairing H^i(X, Q_l) × H^{2d−i}(X, Q_l(d)) → Q_l, for the l-adic (not only torsion) coefficients.

For k algebraically closed and l invertible in k: the l-adic cycle class map CH^r(X) → H^{2r}(X, Q_l(r)) for smooth projective X, compatible with Gysin pullback along morphisms of smooth projective varieties, with proper pushforward (defined through Poincaré duality), with intersection and cup products, and sending the class of a point to an element of trace one.

The hypothesis that a field k admits resolution of singularities, in the sense MVW use (p. 97): every integral scheme of finite type over k has a proper birational map from a smooth scheme, and every proper birational cdh cover of a smooth scheme is refined by a composite of blow-ups with smooth centres; together with Hironaka's theorem that fields of characteristic zero admit it (the named proved setting). Also: platification of a morphism by a blow-up (Raynaud-Gruson), smooth projective compactifications with simple normal crossings boundary in characteristic zero, Nagata compactification of a scheme of finite type, and the deformation to the normal cone of a smooth pair. MC.4 states its conditional results under this hypothesis and MC.5 uses resolution in characteristic zero for its generators; neither plans resolution.

Hard Lefschetz for l-adic cohomology, as DWP.9 states it: for X projective smooth of pure dimension d over an algebraically closed field of characteristic different from l and η = c_1(L) for an ample line bundle L, η^r : H^{d−r}(X, Q_l) → H^{d+r}(X, Q_l)(r) is an isomorphism for every r ≥ 0. MC.7 uses it to define the class inverting η^r, whose algebraicity is the typed Lefschetz standard conjecture, and, through the comparison of SF.6, hard Lefschetz for Betti cohomology over C.

Faltings's isogeny theorem as R28.4 states it: for abelian varieties A, B over a number field F and a prime l, the natural map Hom_F(A, B) ⊗ Q_l → Hom_{G_F}(V_l(A), V_l(B)) is bijective. The register entry of MC.7 for the Tate conjecture for divisors on abelian varieties over number fields is obtained from it through the decomposition NS(A × B) = NS(A) ⊕ NS(B) ⊕ Hom(A, B̂) that Totaro records.

For a smooth projective complex variety X: the algebraic de Rham complex with its truncations Ω^{≥p}, and the isomorphism between algebraic de Rham cohomology and singular cohomology with complex coefficients, compatible with cup products, pullback and trace, as C5 states. MC.7 defines the Hodge filtration on H^n(X(C), C) as the image of the hypercohomology of Ω^{≥p} under this isomorphism.

Chow's theorem as C4 states it: closed analytic subspaces of complex projective space are algebraic. MC.7/cycle-classes-are-hodge uses it to pass from closed analytic subspaces, whose integration currents give the (p, p) type, to algebraic cycles.

restructure.title: MC.2 should own the axioms of a realisation, not the construction of any realisation
restructure.detail: The brief of MC.2 asks both for the axiomatics of cycle class compatibility and for the construction and comparison of the Betti, de Rham and etale realisations. The first is planned here in full, and it is what makes this roadmap the owner of the notion of a realisation: the data, the three axioms, the cohomological pushforward, the Kuenneth decomposition of the diagonal and the equivalence between classical Weil cohomology theories and Q-linear symmetric monoidal functors on motives. The second belongs to the layers that own the cohomology theories: the reviewed audit of SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.2 records that neither pinned library has a named etale cohomology API, constant torsion coefficients or any comparison of cohomology across sites, and SF.6 is the layer the atlas already names for the comparison theorems. Constructing a theory here would plan the same mathematics twice, which PROTOCOL section 15 forbids. The proposal is to narrow MC.2 to the axiomatics and the functorial characterisation, with the theories and their comparisons imported from SF.2 and SF.6; this packet is written to that narrowing and files the two requests that implement it. RS-08 narrowed MC.4 for the same reason and did not reach MC.2.

restructure.title: MC.7 should be divided into a statements sub-layer and a proved-cases register
restructure.detail: MC.7 is asked to do two different things: to give typed statements of open conjectures, which is mathematics this roadmap can own and which needs only a source that states them, and to maintain a register of proved special cases, each of which needs its own primary source and its own hypotheses on the base field, the characteristic, the codimension and the coefficient field. The two have different acceptance tests and different source routes, and mixing them is what makes the layer hard to close: this packet can state Conjecture C and Conjecture D from the sources read but can only report the known cases of Conjecture C on Jannsen's authority, because the three primary papers were not obtained. The proposal is to divide MC.7 into a sub-layer for the statements and the implications between them, and a sub-layer for the register of proved cases with one entry per case and its source. The atlas would then show the conjectures as planets of the first sub-layer, and the register would be a separate piece of work whose progress is visible.

sourceIssues.excerpt: We ﬁrst restrict to the eﬀective situation. Let P eﬀ 1,2 and Aeﬀ 1,2 be the algebras for this diagram. ... Hence by Theorem 2.6 P eﬀ 1,2 = Aeﬀ 1,2 and P1,2 = A1,2.
sourceIssues.correction: On the diagram of all pairs, singular and de Rham cohomology are not graded multiplicative representations, so Theorem 2.6 gives only an isomorphism of vector spaces there. The algebra structure must be taken through the diagram of good pairs, where both cohomologies are graded multiplicative, using the analogue of Corollary 1.7 that the comparison algebras of all pairs and of good pairs agree (which the source invokes only in the proof of Corollary 2.11), and checking that the product of P^+ matches on generators.
sourceIssues.reason: For a pair (X, Y) that is not good, H^{i+i′} of the product pair is the sum over a + b = i + i′ of H^a(X, Y) ⊗ H^b(X′, Y′) and not H^i ⊗ H^{i′}, so the isomorphisms τ of Definition B.14 do not exist; Proposition B.16, Lemma B.21 and Proposition B.22, on which the multiplicative statements rest, all assume a graded multiplicative representation.

sourceIssues.locator: Proof of Theorem 2.6 (page 10), arXiv:1105.0865v5
sourceIssues.printed: By definition P_{1,2} is the subspace of ∏_{p∈D} T_1(p) ⊗ T_2(p)^∨ of elements satisfying the relations induced by D. By definition A_{1,2}(T) is the subspace of ∏_{p∈D} Hom(T_1(p), T_2(p))^∨ of elements satisfying the relations induced by D.
sourceIssues.excerpt: By deﬁnition P1,2 is the subspace of ∏p∈D T1(p) ⊗ T2(p)∨ of elements satisfying the relations induced by D. By deﬁnition A1,2(T ) is the subspace of ∏p∈D Hom(T1(p), T2(p))∨ of elements satisfying the relations induced by D.
sourceIssues.correction: Both are quotients, not subspaces: for finite D, P_{1,2} is the quotient of the sum of the T_1(p) ⊗ T_2(p)^∨ by the span of the elements T_1(f)ω ⊗ γ − ω ⊗ T_2(f)^∨γ, one for each edge f, and A_{1,2} = Hom(T_1|D, T_2|D)^∨ is the quotient of the dual of the product of the Hom(T_1(p), T_2(p)) by the annihilator of the subspace Hom(T_1|D, T_2|D) cut out by the edge conditions, which is the span of the same elements. With 'quotient' the conclusion 'this is the same thing' holds.
sourceIssues.reason: Definition 2.4 presents P_{1,2} by generators and relations, which is a quotient; Definition 2.1 takes the dual of the subspace Hom(T_1|F, T_2|F), which is a quotient of the dual of the ambient product. The elements of the product 'satisfying the relations' form neither space.

review.notes: Four independent reviewers (MC.0–MC.1, MC.2–MC.3, MC.4–MC.5, MC.6–MC.7) checked every node against its source at the cited locator (all recorded SHA-256 values match), every baseline citation at the pinned commits, closure, granularity, API, unit tests, planets and the library audit; RS-08's narrowing of MC.4 was followed. Of the 96 original nodes 5 are verified, 89 corrected and 2 removed (MC.4/cancellation-over-a-perfect-field duplicated MotivicEtaleKTheory M.5a; the Nisnevich-against-etale comparison lies outside MC.4 as RS-08 narrows it); 79 nodes are added; MC.0/homological-equivalence moved to MC.2, since it needs MC.2's Weil cohomology. Baseline: 48 original citations, 39 confirmed (four with no remaining consumer kept as register entries), 9 fixed, 3 removed; 57 added. Source issues: E1–E5 confirmed, E6–E47 added and confirmed, among them errors in stated results of the Stacks Project (0FGR's diagonal formula), Jannsen (the trivial relation) and Huber–Müller-Stach (Lemma 1.12, Theorem 2.6's subspaces). Coverage: MC.1 and MC.3 are source decomposed; MC.0, MC.2, MC.4, MC.5, MC.6 and MC.7 were marked source decomposed with work remaining and are now partial.
